description:
Spin- A Multiformat Movie Marathon, What this is:
The event is a mystery movie marathon where each film plays on a different home media format over 12 hours from 10am to 10pm. There are three distinct sections, times are approximate. The event is R18, nothing is overly controversial but one film is a horror movie rated R18 for violence and nudity. The line up is subject to change but here is an indication:
Film:
Standard 8mm film - 10 minutes
Super 8mm film - 20 minutes
16mm film -90 minute urban adventure
Analog Video:
Betamax - 90 minute horror
VHS - 90 minute action
Laserdisc- 100 minute scifi action 

Digital Video:
VCD- 100 minutes comedy
DVD - 100 minutes ???
HD-DVD TBC
The film will be played on film projectors, the analog video on a CRT video projector (all going well) and the digital video on a digital video projector. All in either mono or glorious 2.0 stereo sound. Most projection is on a 2 meter wide screen.
There will be a half hour break between the analog and digital video sections. And smaller breaks during some format changeovers.
Seating provided will largely be camping chairs, if you want to bring your own chair you can- and there is a reduced ticket price option. This is intended for normal sized chairs, a camping chair, an office chair etc, not a huge armchair. There is limited space where you could bring your own beanbag up front, but you may be staring up at a sharp angle.

What this isn’t:
This is not polished professional event, it's a little bit improvised. We’re not screening in a regular cinema, we’re screening at Valhalla who are very kindly giving us a dark versatile space to work in. Technical issues may arise and we will keep on rolling, discarding formats and entire films in the line up if we can’t get them running. Some things have back ups, some don’t. No refunds, your ticket price is directly funding the event, and the event is an experiment. You can leave at any time, but please don’t yo-yo in and out every few minutes.
The presentation of the films is experimental, but the films for the most part are narrative drama films, not overly inaccessible.
Valhalla is a licensed venue so please do not bring in alcohol- If you do I will ask you to leave- with no refund! That would be awkward for both of us!

“A group of teenage boys compete in an annual contest known as The Long Walk, and keep walking faster than three miles per hour — or risk being shot.”
Early reviews back up claims that this intense and emotional exploration of boyhood is one of the most powerful Stephen King adaptations ever made – one that will stay with you long after you leave the cinema.
Based on King’s 1979 novel, the film is co-written by JT Mollner (‘Strange Darling’) and directed by Francis Lawrence (‘Constantine’, ‘The Hunger Games’ franchise) – features a sensational young cast alongside living legend Mark Hamill as our sinister antagonist.
Come to the cinema early to enjoy our themed lobby and custom pre-show… and don’t forget to drink plenty of water beforehand

Come along and be amongst the first to see NZ feature film Went Up The Hill from queer NZ filmmaker Sam Van Grinsven.

https://www.nziff.co.nz/.../te.../went-up-the-hill/
The film is also screening at NZIFF in centres around the country including Auckland, Christchurch, Dunedin amongst others!
Shot in Canterbury and funded by the NZ Film Commission, the film stars Vicky Krieps (The Phantom Thread) and Dacre Montgomery (Stranger Things) in a poetic ghost story that centres on two queer characters-a woman and her dead wife’s estranged son -as they are each haunted by her spirit. The film premiered to critical acclaim as a Special Presentation at Toronto Film Festival in 2024 where Sam was hailed by Hollywood Reporter as already having the ‘control of a master’ in a film that is ‘captivating', ‘elliptical' and 'technically stunning’.
Sam Van Grinsven has a passion for queer interpretation of genre and seeing queer characters within spaces that historically have not been explored as diversely.

description:
The Antarctic Film Festival - Paekākāriki, An unforgettable evening of storytelling from the coldest place on Earth. The New Zealand Antarctic Society is proud to invite you to a presentation by Georgia Grant and a curated selection of captivating short films from the heart of Antarctica.

The films blend stunning documentary footage, curated by award winning filmmaker Anthony Powell, that reveals the continent’s stark beauty, unforgiving conditions, climate change, and penguin antics with stories captured by inventive and funny entries from the Winter International Film Festival of Antarctica’s 48-Hour Challenge, an annual showcase of creativity and resilience from those who winter-over on the Ice.

But before the films, we'll hear from Georgia Grant who is a sedimentologist within the Earth Sciences Surface Geoscience Department. Her research interests focus on climate variability in recent periods and past warmer climates, including Antarctic Ice Sheet and sea-level change. She analyses the statistical frequency of physical and geochemical characteristics of shallow-marine and deep-marine sediment cores. Come and join us for this informative talk and learn from Georgia's insights.

description:
The Antarctic Film Festival, An unforgettable evening of storytelling from the coldest place on Earth. The New Zealand Antarctic Society is proud to invite you to a presentation by Alexander Hillary and a curated selection of captivating short films from the heart of Antarctica.

The films blend stunning documentary footage, curated by award-winning filmmaker Anthony Powell, that reveals the continent’s stark beauty, unforgiving conditions, climate change, and penguin antics with stories captured by inventive and funny entries from the Winter International Film Festival of Antarctica’s 48-Hour Challenge, an annual showcase of creativity and resilience from those who winter-over on the Ice.

But before the films, we'll hear from Alexander Hillary, who is the General Manager of the Himalayan Trust and a passionate advocate for people, mountains, and remote environments. A lifelong adventurer and environmentalist, Alexander continues the legacy of his grandfather, Sir Edmund Hillary, through work that connects communities, landscapes, and stories across the globe.

At the Antarctic Film Festival, he’ll share his reflections on Antarctica and the Sub-Antarctic, drawing powerful comparisons with Arctic environments and cultures he has encountered, offering a unique perspective on the challenges and beauty of the world's polar regions.

The Big Bike Film Night 2026 - Wellington, The Big Bike Film Night 2026 - Wellington
Let the good times ROLL! The screening sensation known as The Big Bike Film Night is back in '26 for your bike films fix!!!

Sunday 22nd March 5:00pm
Wednesday 25th March 6:30pm
Wednesday 1st April 6:30pm

What's it all about??? The Big Bike Film Night is on a mission- bringing the best cycling short films from around the world together for you.

Showcasing 2.5 hours of riveting bike films that have everything a cycle-centric audience could want - action, drama, humour, and plenty of inspiration; the evening is unashamedly and utterly, utterly, utterly designed and devised to delight the two-wheel devotee!

The 2026 treasure chest of films includes:

• a compelling story about perseverance, showcasing the challenges and triumphs of navigating daily life following a life-altering injury, and how adaptive design has transformed and enriched the journey forward
• a moving movie that follows a father and son’s journey as they take on one of life’s most meaningful milestones- riding a bike together as a family

description:
This Is Congo - Free Screening (Congo Week), Please join us for a free/koha in-person film screening of "This Is Congo", to raise awareness for Congo Week. There will also be an optional group discussion and light snacks provided (feel free to bring your own snacks too).
You can find more info below (including how to support if you can't attend).
NOTE: As we will be viewing and discussing potentially sensitive topics, this event will have an Open Door Policy. You may leave the venue at any time, for any reason, and will not be judged for doing so.
ABOUT THE DOCUMENTARY FILM:
"A whistle-blower, a patriotic military commander, a mineral dealer, and a displaced tailor share a glimpse of life amid Africa's longest continuing conflict."
WHAT IS CONGO WEEK?
Congo Week is on 19-25 October, where we commemorate the millions of lives lost in this ongoing genocide in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It is also a time to celebrate the enormous humanity and environmental potential the beautiful country DRC has.
WHY ARE WE HOSTING THIS IN TE WHANGANUI-A-TARA, AOTEAROA (WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND)?
We are holding community film screenings during Congo Week to talk to each other as a community, and to help each other learn. As we support other causes/issues in Aotearoa/NZ and worldwide, we would like to increase solidarity for Congolese people.
We are buying, consuming, and benefitting from tech products/AI usage through child slavery and genocide of Congo. As long as there are customers of minerals found in the DRC, corporations will have an incentive to continue exploiting Congolese people for these minerals to be used in jewellery, batteries, e-cigarettes, and tech products like our phones and computers.
HOW MUCH IS THE TICKET?
The film screening is free but we appreciate koha for the Panzi Foundation (more info below).
WHY WOULD I WANT TO JOIN THE FILM SCREENING?
The film screening is for anyone keen to learn/watch a documentary film, wants to share their experience through optional group discussion, or wants to meet new people.
This event welcomes people from all walks of life who are willing to learn, listen, or contribute (LGBTQ+ friendly).
Before 7:45pm: Set up
7:45-8pm: Karakia, health and safety, organisers' introductions, brief explanation on Congo Week
8pm-9:30pm: "This Is Congo" screening (people can come and go at any time)
9:30pm-9:40pm: Moment of silence/meditation
9:40pm-10pm: Quick group discussion with optional participation (TBC if we can extend)
By 10pm: Pack down
WILL THERE BE MORE IN-PERSON/VIRTUAL FILM SCREENINGS IN THE FUTURE?
Yes, will most likely be in 2026 instead of this year. We would love to collaborate with other people/groups, so we can share our skills and knowledge collectively.
I CAN'T ATTEND. HOW CAN I SUPPORT?
Please spread the word via social media stories, reposting, wheatpasting, or sharing to people who don't use social media (Instagram post here).
If you click RSVP, there is an option to donate without getting a ticket. We sincerely appreciate this.
You can RSVP to the 22 Oct 2025 film screening here.
If you click "Contact host" below, feel free to send us your email address and we can email resources after the event, e.g.:
Use refurbished tech products (instead of new ones)
Alternatives to Google/Microsoft mail/maps/calendar/forms/etc
Alternatives to Spotify/Apple Music
Reducing generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) usage at work/personal life
If using Google as your search engine, add "-ai" at the end of your searches (to stop showing AI results)
Actions and Instagram accounts to follow
WHERE WILL THE KOHA GO TOWARDS?
Koha that we receive will go to the Panzi Foundation.
The Panzi Foundation has opened hospitals, mobile clinics, and the City of Joy, a sanctuary where women learn healing, empowerment and leadership through their traumas. Rape is a weapon of war used against the Congolese people.
The Panzi Foundation is one of the largest African-led nonprofits and is committed to addressing the devastating impacts of sexual and gender based violence through a holistic, survivor-centred approach.
The Panzi Foundation was founded by Dr. Denis Mukwege, who is considered one of the leading experts in injuries of rape and was awarded a Nobel Peace Prize in 2018, 6 years after an assassination attempt on his life.
WHO ARE THE EVENT ORGANISERS?
This event is organised by ordinary community members affiliated with Te Tai-Tētēkura (an indigenous, youth-led group in Aotearoa/NZ).
Te Tai-Tētēkura is founded on the principles of revolution through education and restoration of power to the people. They hold a foundational community-based kaupapa that prioritises uplifting, connecting, and empowering our communities.
Te Tai-Tētēkura's founding is based on the socialist and revolutionary politics of the Black Panther Party, which rose to prominence during the Black Power Movement in the U.S. They combine the Black Panther Party's ideas with Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and their own landback and decolonisation principles.
Through community initiatives, Te Tai-Tētēkura shows the people that we as a community can take care of our society.
We stand in solidarity with indigenous peoples in Aotearoa/NZ, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and across the world facing injustice.
Please click "Contact host" if you have questions/feedback/concerns or if you can't attend anymore.

description:
Toitu: Visual Sovereignty film screening, Toi Tū Toi Ora: Contemporary Māori Art was the largest Māori exhibition in the history of Auckland Art Gallery and attracted attendance levels not seen by the gallery since 1989. Chelsea Winstanley’s documentary follows the journey of curator Nigel Borell as he navigates the constraints between institutional authority and Māori self-determination.
Chelsea Winstanley’s documentary follows the journey of curator Nigel Borell as he navigates the constraints between institutional authority and Māori self-determination. Borell’s curatorial vision is clear – Māori art must be authored, not simply advocated for. For the artists, this represents a chance to be seen on their own terms and is an initiative that ultimately leads some to the global stage of the Venice Biennale. 
But as the scale of the exhibition grows, so does the institutional resistance. The result is a reckoning: whose story is being told, and who holds the pen? With many of the artworks exploring the legacy of colonialism, the making of the exhibition itself becomes a living reflection of that very struggle. Laying bare behind-the-scenes conversations rarely seen on screen, TOITŪ Visual Sovereignty lifts the curtain on the inner workings of an institution and examines the cost of visibility without control – and the quiet power of walking away. — Heperi Mita 
The screening will be followed by a Q and A with Director Chelsea Winstanley.

description:
Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me, "Faster and faster. And for a long time you wouldn't feel anything. And then you'd burst into fire" - Laura Palmer
TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME.
DAVID LYNCH | USA & FRANCE | 1992 | 135mins | R18+| 4K DCP PROVIDED BY JANUS FILMS DISTRIBUTION
Join us for this very special community fundraiser screening of the prequel to the critically acclaimed series, "Twin Peaks".
ABC cancelled the original series after season 2 but a month later, Lynch announced he was "not yet finished with the material" and principal photography for the full length prequel film, began on September 5th 1991 at a caravan site in Snoqualmie Washington. Which became the "Fat Trout Trailer Park" where the story of the last 7 days of Laura Palmer begins.
Since its showing at the 1992 Festival De Cannes, no other Lynch film had polarized audiences to such an extent. Fans that wanted more "Cherry Pie" and "Donuts" from the TV show were served a much darker, unflinching and unforgiving work - in Lynch's own words, a movie about "the loneliness, shame, guilt, confusion and devastation of the victim". Derided by critics and many fans at the time it was a commercial box office flop.
Yet in the years since the initial reaction, a gradual wave of reappraisal and appreciation began. With time it's brilliance came into focus with growing acknowledgment, that the film is a more accurate, complex and powerful account of trauma. Combining the dramatic ferocity of Sherly Lee's tour de force and the beauty of Angelo Badalamenti's score, Lynch reclaimed full ownership of the material creating a harrowing, compassionate and enigmatic hymn to Laura Palmer.
As we approach the films 34 year anniversary and since Lynch's passing in 2025, it is now regarded by critics and fans worldwide, as a revered epilogue, essential predecessor to "The Return", and Lynch's most chilling, terrifying, and yet empathetic and humane cinematic masterpiece.

After sold-out shows in May 2025, we’re bringing back Never Forgotten: The Marines of Masterton for one more special screening in Martinborough!

This feature-length local documentary tells the story of the United States Marine Corps’ 3rd Defense Battalion, who were stationed at Solway Showgrounds in Masterton in 1943 during World War II. Director Mark Pacey explores the Marines’ visit, the deep connections they formed with the local community, and their lasting legacy—including the journey to constructing a memorial in their honour.

Presented by Waifilmfest in partnership with Circus Cinema, Restaurant & Bar and the Wellington Historical Festival 2025, this is a unique opportunity to experience a powerful story of history, community, and remembrance.

Wairarapa Cinémathèque 2026 Presents METROPOLIS (1927), Metropolis (1927)
Sunday 5 April 2026, 7:30pm
Dir. Fritz Lang | Germany | 2h 3m | Silent | Sci-Fi | Drama

A towering achievement of early cinema, Metropolis is Fritz Lang’s visionary silent masterpiece: a film that continues to shape how we imagine the future.

Set in a vast, futuristic city sharply divided between privileged elites and oppressed workers, the story follows the ruler’s son as he meets Maria, a prophetic young woman who calls for understanding and compassion between the classes. What unfolds is an extraordinary spectacle of monumental design, groundbreaking special effects, and a deeply human moral vision.

Both epic and intimate, Metropolis is a powerful meditation on class, technology, and empathy. It is one of the most influential films ever made.

This special screening of METROPOLIS is presented in cooperation with the Goethe-Institut New Zealand.

Join the Wairarapa Cinémathèque. Memberships are available now, giving access to a curated programme of classic and significant films throughout 2026. Wairarapa Cinémathèque is dedicated to celebrating film as part of our artistic and cultural heritage. We value the communal experience of cinema, bringing people together through curated screenings, discussions, and the sharing of films of significance. Wairarapa Cinémathèque 2026 presents SOME LIKE IT HOT (1959), SOME LIKE IT HOT (1959)
Dir. Billy Wilder | USA | 2h | Comedy, Romance, Crime

After witnessing a Mafia hit, two Chicago musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) flee the city disguised as women in an all-female jazz band bound for Florida. Chaos, romance, and mistaken identity follow; including Marilyn Monroe at her most luminous.

Hilarious, subversive, and endlessly quotable, Some Like It Hot is widely regarded as one of the greatest comedies ever made. Billy Wilder’s razor-sharp wit, dazzling performances, and audacious gender play still feel astonishingly fresh more than 65 years on.

This screening opens the 2026 Wairarapa Cinémathèque season.

WAIRARAPA CINÉMATHÈQUE 2026
Celebrating 100 Years of Film

Wairarapa Cinémathèque is a membership-based film programme dedicated to cinema as art, heritage, and shared experience. We believe films are meant to be seen together on the big screen and talked about afterwards.

In 2026, as cinema marks its centenary, our programme brings together restored classics, silent cinema, epic dramas, and contemporary masterpieces that continue to resonate today.

Screenings take place on the first Sunday of each month at 7:30pm
Regent Theatre, Masterton (now Regent 3 Cinemas)

The Cinémathèque operates independently under non-commercial screening rights, fostering a welcoming community of local cinephiles.

Our first live panel event takes place in Wellington and opens with a discussion exploring the history, legacy, successes, and ongoing challenges of being a screenwriter in Aotearoa New Zealand. This panel brings together practitioners, academics, and critics, and will reflect on the role of film and television in helping us understand ourselves and each other.
Does film and television give us the chance to examine our values and culture? If the answer to this question is yes, then how are we doing? What have our stories on screen had to say about us in the past, and what are they saying about us now?

Dana Leaming

In September, we'll get back on track, away from the International Whiskies of our August tasting, and on to the Eastern Highlands of Scotland: Glendronach.
Named for the valley of the brambles surrounding the distillery, Glendronach was the second distillery to gain a legal whisky license, and is currently under the stewardship of Dr. Rachel Barrie, a legend in the whisky industry. Dr Barrie has recently revamped the Glendronach lineup, and we're going to see how she's doing: we'll try the previous 12 and 15 year--old bottlings against her new releases. She's worked her magic at Ben Riach, and we'll see how she's doing at Glendronach (I suspect quite well!). Additionally, we'll try the highland peated Glendronach, a departure from the familiar smokey peat of Islay. We'll expect a sweeter, softer style, bolstered by some sherry maturation.

Join Steve Logan and Shaun Clouston, alongside original Logan Brown team members Francois Febvre (La Cloche) and Shepherd Elliott (previously of Ti Kouka, Leeds Street Bakery, Shepherd, Concord and The Test Kitchen), for a special afternoon filled with fantastic kai and plenty of memories.

As the doors of Logan Brown first opened in 1996, it quickly became one of Wellington’s most beloved dining destinations. Now, this unforgettable event offers a chance to reminisce with the chefs who helped shape the restaurant’s legacy, sharing tales from the early days while serving up a feast of flavours inspired by their storied careers.

For any longtime Logan Brown fan or someone curious to the whakapapa of Wellington food, this is a celebration of the friendships, milestones, and moments that have defined one of New Zealand’s most iconic dining experiences. Expect a menu that reflects Logan Brown’s rich history, prepared with passion and paired with great conversation, laughter, and a few tall tales.

description:
A Night on the Orient Express, All aboard as The Botanist turns into The Orient Express. Your tasty train journey will begin in Paris, heading to Istanbul via Germany, Austria, Serbia, Hungary and Bulgaria. The 7-course menu features modern plant-based takes on traditional dishes from each country’s cuisine, such as French crepes with vegan duck a l'orange, coconut-crusted parsnip Austrian schnitzel and Bulgarian kashkaval house-made cultured cashew cheese and spinach pastry; paired with creative cocktails, live music and some iconic Orient Express touches.
 
7-course tasting menu. Matched cocktails (alcoholic or non-alchoholic) can be added to your ticket.

Get ready for a full-throttle feast: a rustic 6-course beer and food pairing at Panhead, led by our Innovation Brewer Bern and Bar Boss Bree. We’re talking bold brews, killer eats, and some behind the scenes insights during a flavour filled evening.

description:
A Taste of Newtown- Kai celebration, Come and join us for our 7th annual Newtown Community Meal, hosted at Newtown School, a celebration of the incredible diversity, creativity, and collaboration that makes our suburb so special.
This is a shared meal that truly reflects Newtown, featuring food that has been grown, sourced, foraged, and prepared right here in our community. Together we’ll enjoy an abundance of amazing kai, including homemade dumplings, locally foraged preserves, and bountiful salads made from locally grown produce.
This event is about celebrating the very best of our suburb, our people, our cultures, and the food that brings us together. Everyone is welcome, so please bring your whānau, friends, and neighbours.
Doors will open at 3pm with music, snacks and time to connect with your neighbours. The main meal will be served at 4.30pm
As always, this is a koha-based event. You’re invited to contribute what you can, but most importantly, we’d love to see you there and share a meal together.
We can’t wait to celebrate Newtown with you.

description:
Alexia Pizza Nights with Roving Pizza, On occasional Friday evenings Alexia is doing a little pizza pop-up with Roving Pizza!

Roving Pizza make beautiful wood-fired Napoletana style pizzas. Fresh spins on authentic Italian flavours with delightfully soft and crunchy bases achieved through a 24-hour dough fermentation process. All handmade, using the best ingredients, cooked in front of you. Delicious!

How it works:

• Alexia is open from 4pm – 8pm. Pizzas are available to order 4.15pm – 7.00pm or until sold out. Bar snacks and a little sweet finish are also available.
• No bookings taken – just turn up and find a spot. If the weather is nice we’ll be on the terrace and lawn. If the weather is not so nice we’ll be on the terrace and in the winery (all covered).
• Takeaway pizza is also available, walk-in only - no email/phone orders. You need to turn up to order your pizza. Enjoy a glass of Alexia while you wait, and grab a bottle of something delicious to take home.
• Apologies but Roving Pizza does not currently offer gluten free pizza bases. GF and want to join in the fun? We have some GF food options available.
• No BYO food/drinks.

description:
Alexia Urban Winery Presents Bonjour Gimlet!, Alexia Urban Winery Presents Bonjour Gimlet! (A Sparkling French Affair)

Alexia is bringing a touch of France to Greytown with their sparkliest cocktail yet…the Alexia Bonjour Gimlet!

Sure, the original gin and lime juice Gimlet was invented by British Royal Navy surgeon Sir Thomas Gimlette to prevent navy sailors getting scurvy, but it was the French who made it classy with the addition of elderflower liqueur.

Alexia is taking their Gimlet a step further, giving it an effervescent twist – combining Greytown Distilling gin, the floral notes of elderflower liqueur, and fresh lime juice… then topping it off with Alexia Blanc de Noirs Méthode Traditionnelle. With a French-themed food menu to match, this is a Gimlet worth saying Bonjour to!

The French flags will be flying, the croque monsieurs will be magnifique, and the berets will be positioned at the jauntiest angle possible! This is your call to cancel all boring plans for March 21 and say ‘oui!’ to an afternoon of French joie de vivre at Alexia!

Alexia will donate $4 from each Bonjour Gimlet sold towards fundraising efforts for the New Zealand Festival of Christmas.

Essential details: 12pm – 5pm, Saturday 21 March, Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown. No bookings required, just turn up. Dogs ok. GF? Yes. This is a rain-or-shine event, so don’t miss out!

The Greytown International Cocktail Festival is proudly sponsored by Greytown Distilling Co and The White Swan.

description:
Arizona Flashback, Dust off the denim, dig out the flip phones and get ready to rewind time. Two Grey is bringing back Arizona Bar & Grill for a limited-time pop-up.

Welcome to The Arizona Flashback, a throwback to the late '90s and early 2000s that revives the flavours, energy and atmosphere of the iconic Arizona Bar & Grill. Known as a go-to spot for after-work drinks, late-night bites, birthday celebrations and casual catch-ups, Arizona was a place where people came together over great food and good times.

Now, its beloved Southwestern-style dishes and all-day menu return — not just as a delicious nod to the past, but as a celebration of shared moments, laughter and connection.

Immerse yourself in the full Y2K dining experience, complete with retro beats, neon lights and the return of Arizona’s famous Spin the Wheel game for a dash of playful nostalgia.

description:
Ata Rangi Summer Sessions - Auckland Anniversary Saturday, Head to Martinborough wine village for another epic Summer Session at Ata Rangi.

DJ OG Masala brings the sunny, summer grooves while renowned NZ seafood legend Martin Bosley will be serving a menu built for hot days and cold wine, including: Ika Mata (coconut-marinated fish with totopos), Whitebait fritters, Sashimi, Pāua fritters tucked between slices of soft white bread!

Entry is free - pay to play - with all food and beverages purchased on consumption. Boz has designed dishes to pair beautifully with Ata Rangi wines. This is a Saturday Session that you won’t want to miss.

What to expect: A welcoming afternoon of:
- Bubbles, rosé, and summer-favourite Ata Rangi wines
- Shade, sunshine, and space to relax
- Exceptional local seafood
- Music that keeps the day humming

No ticket required - but please RSVP so we can cater accordingly. visit@atarangi.co.nz

This is part of a series of four Ata Rangi Summer Sessions, taking place on 17 Jan, 24 Jan, 7 Feb and 21 Feb. See the full series at www.atarangi.com/ata-rangi-events

description:
Aurora Distillery Gin Experience, Create, make and take home your own gin with us at our Gin Experience sessions at our beautiful Wairarapa site, just 10 minutes from Martinborough. Our experienced distillery staff are on hand throughout to guide you through the process and give as much or as little advice as you want. We have hundreds of satisfied customers who have made some really exciting gins.

You’ll begin by foraging in the distillery gardens then we move to the gin-making room to learn about the gin making process and the ingredients involved. You’ll sample loads of botanicals then you will choose what you want to put in your very own gin recipe. After weighing out your recipe, you’ll move to your very own still and begin distilling!

While your gin is distilling, we’ll do a gin tasting of some of our own Arrival brand gins and some surprises from our other spirits.

At the end of the session you’ll bottle and seal your own 500ml bottle of gin to take home!

Please note each Experience attendee must have their own ticket. To ensure all participants have a great time and get our full attention we cannot accept spectators.

description:
Bar Blanc de Blancs with Martin Bosley's Oyster Saloon, Alexia's special annual Blanc de Blancs celebration returns for a 4th edition with the release of the 2021 vintage of our world famous (in Greytown) Méthode Traditionnelle!

After four years of patient making and aging, the corks on the most sparkly of all our wines are ready to be popped and the liquid gold consumed on the Alexia terrace!

The man, the myth, the mollusc maestro Martin Bosley is back with his Oyster Saloon between 12pm - 3pm shucking fresh oysters for the occasion so get in early for these or miss out!

Oysters not your thing? Fear not, the Alexia kitchen will also be turning out some delicious delights to match to your Blanc de Blancs – everyone will be happy!

It’s always a great day when the new vintage of Blanc de Blancs starts flowing and we’re quietly delighted with how the 2021 vintage is looking!

Essential Details:
- Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown.
- Leashed dogs ok!
- No bookings required, just turn up. Want oysters? Get there before 3pm.
- Parking onsite, on the street, and lots of parking for bikes. 15 minute walk from Greytown centre.

description:
Barnardos Foundation Gala Dinner, Be part of an extraordinary evening at the inaugural Barnardos Foundation Gala Dinner, proudly presented by Willis Bond and LT McGuinness, where generosity, leadership, and purpose come together to create brighter futures for children and families across Aotearoa.

This special event will bring together passionate supporters, business and community leaders, and advocates for change for an evening of fine dining, inspiring guest speakers, and exclusive live and silent auction experiences.

Every ticket, bid, and connection made on the night supports the Barnardos Foundation and the wider work of Barnardos Aotearoa, helping fund innovation, research, and services that shift the dial for tamariki and whānau where the need is greatest. Join us to connect, be inspired, and help every child shine bright.

description: Breakfast Club, For one morning only – Loosie’s Superette is opening for breakfast, serving a comfort-filled menu with banging tunes and endless caffeine. Think trayfuls of fluffy pancakes, bacon and egg muffins, crispy hash browns drowned in maple syrup, and bottomless drip coffee to keep things rolling. Add a cheeky mimosa or two, and you’ve got the perfect start to your weekend. Whether you’re with your brunch crew, shaking off a hangover, or chasing the crispy bits, this is a morning made for indulgence. It’s all about good food, loud laughs, and that first sip of something strong with your best mates by your side. No rules, no rush - just tunes pumping, trays piling up, and that warm, familiar feeling of a proper brunch done right.

description:
Chance Luck & Magic 2024 Release, Be the first to taste Chance, Luck & Magic 2024, the latest iteration of one of our proudest achievements.

On Saturday 18 October, you can come and taste the beer in our Wild Workshop, the place where it was made. Brewers Pete and Dave will be on hand from 2pm to raise the first toast and tell you all a little about how this year’s blend came to be. We’ll also pull a couple of other goodies from the cellar to keep you and CLM company.

And, to top it off, our friends at Nomames Tacos will be here for the edible pairings.

This beer is the ultimate expression of Wild Workshop’s inner-city terroir, and the 2024 bottle is no different; a blend of five years of 100% spontaneously fermented brews, aged in French oak. The result is a complex and truly unique drop that harnesses the natural character of Pōneke.

We love this beer, and we’re so chuffed that other people do too - we’re very honoured that Chance, Luck & Magic, in its various vintages, has garnered global recognition and become one of our most prestigious creations:
Silver medals at both the 2023 and 2024 World Beer Cup (huge!)
Four consecutive gold medals at the New Zealand Beer Awards, as well as two trophies for Champion European Ale, and the Champion Beer title in 2022
Champion International Beer at the 2024 Australian International Beer Awards

The release of each new edition has become a landmark annual event for us, a chance to take a moment and appreciate the beautiful things that come from the wild workings of the environment.

Come and celebrate with us!
label: Food & Drink

Cheesy Lovers by Le Marché Français, Calling all cheese lovers!
Looking for a fun and original night out for two? Whether it’s a romantic date, a chill evening with a friend, or a cozy family moment, our Cheesy Lovers workshop is the perfect plan

description:
Club Tropicana, This August, Beach Babylon becomes Club Tropicana, a retro, romantic escape inspired by 1960s tropical honeymoons, classic tiki bars and vintage beach glamour. Picture golden sunsets, flamingos, thatched umbrellas and the carefree buzz of a sun-soaked getaway, right in the heart of Wellington. No passport required.

The menu is vibrant and full of escapist flair. Start with coconut prawns and banana blossom kokoda, then dive into mains like mango glazed  pork rib rack or the tropical tofu paneer curry. Save room for dessert: pineapple upside-down pudding or a coconut rum fondue to bring the tropical fantasy to a sweet finale. Behind the bar, the tiki and kava-spiked cocktails flow freely, from Blue Hawaiian’s to retro rum punches, all dressed to impress with flamingo stirrers, umbrellas and tropical garnishes.

A golden-age soundtrack sets the mood, featuring the smooth calypso of Harry Belafonte, beachy vibes from The Beach Boys, and sun-drenched classics by Astrud Gilberto.

Club Tropicana is a winter getaway, fun and fabulously over the top.

description:
DILLI-24, A North Indian feast crafted by long-time Loretta head chef Chandrika Khullar.
Named after her hometown of Delhi and her home postcode, this special menu is a deeply personal tribute to her upbringing and a childhood immersed in the rich culinary traditions of North India. Chandrika brings the heart and soul of Delhi to Wellington with a generous, share-style multi-course menu featuring bountiful vegetarian plates and an exceptional lamb raan.

Expect an explosion of flavour, with exotic spice blends, saffron, citrus and native berries woven into every dish. In North India, condiment is king, and this feast will be served with a vibrant array of chutneys, pickles and relishes. To complete the experience, Chandrika has also designed a beautifully curated drinks menu to complement the bold and fragrant dishes.

description:
Discover Te Muna - Explore the Wines, Te Muna means secret place in Maori. We want to let you into the secret of the Te Muna Valley wines.

Te Muna valley, just east of Martinborough, is not the easiest place to grow grapes. The winds and the temperatures test us.  But the micro climate and the unique soil structure help us produce exceptional wines with a distinctive style.

Join us for a small group, interactive tasting led by wine writer and educator Joelle Thomson, as we explore a curated selection of Te Muna wines from a variety of producers. Craggy Range, Escarpment, Big Sky, Blue Earth Estate and more.

You will be picked up from the Square in Martinborough and driven to the stunning Craggy Range Te Muna Estate vineyard where Joelle will guide you through a tasting of twelve of Te Muna wines. The experience concludes with a relaxed opportunity to revisit some of your favourites from the tasting while meeting several of the producers, before being transported back to the Square.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Discover Te Muna - Go Behind the Scenes in April, Join us for a full-day immersive experience in the viticulture, winemaking and wines of Te Muna Valley. Walk the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste exceptional wines right where they are made.

Tickets are limited to twenty people to ensure that this is an intimate experience, taking you to places that are not normally open to the public.

Your tour begins with pickup from Martinborough Square, leading to a special start at Big Sky Wines. Kath and Jeremy will take you through a hands-on experience of their vineyard and winery. From there, visit the stunning Blue Earth Estate vineyard and olive grove. Margaret and Mike will entertain you with stories of their journey and explain how they grow their olives and grapes. You will then indulge in a long, relaxed lunch accompanied with a glass of wine. Some of the region's winemakers will join us to share their stories and answer your questions. The adventure continues with an insiders' look at the state of the art winery at Escarpment. Rowan will walk you through the process of how grapes are transformed into their wines. The day will conclude with a final tasting in Craggy Range’s private venue at their Te Muna Estate vineyard, where you will have the opportunity to revisit some of your favourite wines and chat with your hosts.

description:

This spectacular valley lies nine kilometres east of Martinborough. Visit the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste the wines where they are made.

We will pick you up from the Martinborough Square at 9.30 am to start your day at Big Sky Wines. Founders, viticulturists, and winemakers Katherine Jacobs and Jeremy Corban will give you a first look at their 2025 ferments, which have been produced from their organic vineyard. We will then take you to tour Blue Earth Estate vineyard and olive grove and enjoy a long lunch, accompanied by a glass of wine of course. From there we will take you to the stunning winery at Escarpment, and then to explore the beautiful terraced Craggy Range vineyard and taste their wines among the vines, both of which are not normally open to the public. We will finish the day with some of the other Te Muna producers joining us to share their wines and their stories. It will be a day of discovery - the place, the people and the wines of the beautiful Te Muna Valley.

description:
Dragons Is My Uso, Chef Jessica Tang and legendary home chefs Litia Lefaoseu and Iutita Mallon are drawing on the century long fusion of Chinese and Samoan cuisine and the way food expresses love, ai, and alofa. In the late 1800s, small numbers of Chinese settled in Samoa and became part of a growing multicultural community. There they influenced local customs, made an enduring contribution to Samoan cuisine introducing contemporary favourites such as sapasui (chop suey), keke pua‘a (pork buns) and of course laisa (rice). 

Dragons celebrate this cultural and culinary fusion by showcasing these favourites and presenting new dishes highlighting the shared love of culinary staples such as taro and noodles, rice, fish, and pork, the magnificent spectrum of Chinese herbs, spices and flavours. Through cooking and sharing food together the chefs honour their culinary heritage, strengthen our connections to one another and celebrate the big and little moments in life. This is a shared-style meal, served banquet style on lazy Susan turntables. 
Dragons is My Uso was one of the sell-out hits of the 2024 festival - don't miss out!

Raised in Sardinia and now at home in New Zealand, Chef Ricatti shares his story through a menu that bridges the wild, untouched landscapes of both countries. Each course is crafted exclusively with New Zealand ingredients, reflecting the rich bounty of our land and sea, yet inspired by the timeless traditions and bold flavours of Sardinian cuisine.

Accompanying the meal is an expertly selected pairing of wines from Sardinia and New Zealand, highlighting the unique characteristics of each region while celebrating their shared essence. The thoughtful combination of food and drink creates a dialogue between the two islands, offering diners a chance to taste the harmony of contrasts.

More than just a meal, this is an evening of storytelling. Chef Ricatti invites you to journey with him as he reflects on the places that have shaped his life and the meaning of finding a home across oceans. His philosophy of embracing the present moment is woven into every dish, making this event a sensory and emotional experience.

Whether you’re a lover of fine dining, an admirer of Sardinian culture, or simply curious about the connections between food and identity, this dinner promises a night of discovery. Step into the heart of two islands and savour their soul in one unforgettable evening.

description:
Fat Queers Eating Cake, There’s so much strength and solidarity in members of marginalised communities getting together to have a joyous good time. Fat Queers Eating Cake! is a shared meal (please bring food to share, if you’re able), where you can gather with friends old and new, free of any diet talk or body shaming.

WHO
This is an event for you if you’re fat, any gender and any flavour of queer. Please be assured that fat is absolutely a neutral term referring to body size in the same way that tall or brunette are also neutral terms. It’s our word to use how we like - just like queer.

There’s no tape measure at the door to determine if you’re ‘fat enough’, we just ask that smaller fats acknowledge they may have more privilege in various ways than larger fats.

Kids: We don’t want childcare to be a barrier to attending, but this event is not specifically designed for children.

Allies: if you don’t have fat and/or queer friends to bring with you, and you’d be worried about coming alone, feel free to bring one ally with you.

WHAT
Think of it as an inside picnic (which isn’t weather-dependent and is more accessible for those who might not be able to sit on the ground). Bring some food, pop a label on it so those with dietary requirements can nibble safely, make yourself a cuppa and grab a seat!

This event is absolutely free. We ask you to bring some kai to share if you’re able, but if you can’t, please don’t let that stop you from attending.

FOOD
We use cake in the event title because it’s got a decadent ‘sinful’ reputation it’s fun to subvert, but all food is good food, so bring whatever makes you happy. Love to bake? Excellent, we’re into that. Garden overloaded with veges? Bring those! Learned to make amazing hummus because you don’t support genocide? Lovely! Only got time to pass by a dairy? Grab some potato chips. We will have ingredient labels to put with your food.

Please note: During the event, what you eat is your business, what anyone else eats is their business. The only kind of comments appropriate would be “oh this __ is so delicious” NOT “oh I couldn’t eat that, I’d have to go to the gym”.

WHERE
It will be held at Pride HQ - A Hub for Queers. Exact details TBC.

WHY
I used to organise fat liberation events with my ethical clothing company House of Boom. I’ve folded that now, but still want to help provide spaces for our community to get together, have some fun, and work to overturn fatphobic bullshit at the same time. Now that I've joined the board of Wellington Pride, specifically to help make events more accessible to the 1 in 3 members of the Rainbow Community who are disabled, I thought this would be a particularly fitting event to host. Join us!

I-Sarn Thai KanTok, Join Daeng from Tuk Tuk Thai for a deeply personal culinary journey to the heart of E-Sarn, the north-eastern region of Thailand she once called home. This one-night-only event celebrates the traditional Kan-Tok style of dining – a communal meal served on handwoven bamboo trays and shared amongst family and friends. This event is made to be shared, the ticket price is for a shared menu for two. 

Growing up in the small town of Tha Bo near the Mekong Delta, Daeng’s childhood was filled with stories of rice farming, village generosity, and dishes cooked from what the garden offered. In E-Sarn, meals were acts of love, shared daily around the Kan-Tok with laughter, music, and warmth.

Now, Daeng invites you to gather at her table and experience the flavours of her upbringing. You’ll be served nine traditional dishes on a beautifully crafted bamboo tray, designed for sharing, just as they are in her village.

On the Kan-Tok:
Hor Mok Salmon – Steamed salmon in banana leaves, marinated with herbs, spices, and coconut milk
Mok Nor Mai with Pork Belly – Pork belly steamed with bamboo shoots
Larb Gai – A celebratory chicken mince salad with fresh herbs and toasted rice

Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar, Alexia Urban Winery x Greytown Distilling Company present: Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar

Aperitivo – it’s the Italian pre-dinner beverage ritual designed to open the palate, open the stomach, and open the conversation.

Wander past any Italian bar as the sun goes down, and you’ll see the locals sipping martinis and negronis, while engaged in animated discussion!

The common ingredient in these cocktails…and conversations is vermouth – a delicious, aromatic, botanical-loaded, fortified wine. Wine, you say? That’s where we come in. Alexia has been working with Greytown Distilling to create a vermouth for them right here in Greytown, and they’ve asked us to host something fun to celebrate its release for the Greytown International Cocktail Festival!

We’re channelling vermouths Italian roots and transforming into a little pop-up Italian neighbourhood vermouth bar!

We’ll be serving the most intriguing (and cutest) cocktail flight in town to showcase the beauty and versatility of vermouth… the ‘vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray’ - a cocktail broken into three micro parts: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni.

All the Alexia wines will be available too, of course, and it’s Italian all the way in the kitchen, with guest chef Caleb Kloeg turning out crispy arancini and gelato soft-serves so delicious you’ll be transported to Italy.

Cocktail inspired? You’re in luck. Greytown Distilling will have a little pop-up shop on the night, selling all the essential cocktail-making accessories too.

It’s neighbourhood Italian bar vibes on a Greytown backstreet, and we can’t wait… so get on your vespas, pump up the tyres on your Bianchi, rev those Fiats and get to Alexia!

Vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray

The most intriguing cocktail in town…a single cocktail broken into a micro-flight showcasing the beauty and versatility of vermouth: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni. Shrunken, not stirred…

Essential details: 4pm – 8pm, Friday 27 March, Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown. No bookings required, just turn up. GF? Yes. Vegan? Yes. Leashed dogs ok. This is a rain or shine event, so don’t miss out!

description:
Mischief Night Murder Mystery Feast with Chef Max Gordy, 30 October, 🎃 Step inside, if you dare... on the eve of Halloween. It's a Mischief Night* full of tricks and frights!
👻 A chilling murder mystery unfolds over a hauntingly good three-course Halloween dinner by Chef Max Gordy.
Gather your cleverest friends... who will crack the case first: the detectives or the villains?
Expect twists, laughter, and a touch of fright, with spot prizes through the night — plus a reward for the best-dressed.
🍽️ Award-winning chef Max Gordy (Graze Wine Bar) will conjure up a frightfully delicious Halloween-themed feast.
🥂 Your ticket includes one complimentary alcoholic beverage (with more available to purchase on the night).
TICKET TYPES
Round up your squad of six to solve the mystery and devour a fiendishly good feast for $666.
Have a frightening four-some? Book a table for $444.
Spooky single seats available for $111... we will seat you at a mystery table for some mischief!
VENUE
60 Dixon Street is up a flight of steep steps – with only one way in.
FUNDRAISING
Every ticket sold helps Kaibosh ensure that no good food is left to die.  
By joining us for this night of spooky fun, you’ll be directly helping us rescue quality surplus kai and get it to those who need it most.
*What is Mischief Night? In parts of Pennsylvania and New Jersey in the eastern USA, 30 October is called “Mischief Night.” The tradition refers to the eve of Halloween in which children and teenagers celebrate the holiday one night early with pranks, tricks and more. While in New England, some call it Cabbage Night...
Join us to experience Chef Max Gordy's culinary take on Mischief Night in Pōneke!

Now, you can learn the secrets behind their mouthwatering scones firsthand.

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through mixing and preparing your own batch of Pravda’s famous cheese scones. Once your dough is ready, you'll hand them off to be baked to crispy flaky perfection. While they cook, relax with a cup of tea or coffee, and once your scones are ready, you’ll enjoy the fruits of your labour fresh from the oven.

But fear not, I promise we won’t be getting too scientific - and we’ll taste an interesting mix of official and independently bottled crackers, across a multitude of ages from some all-time fave distilleries; Mortlach, Benrinnes, Bunnahabhain and Amrut.
Here’s the lineup…
Bunnahabhain 12 years old 2023 Cask Strength Edition 60.1% (Sherry casks) WB 87.27
Mortlach 'Signatory Symington's Choice' 2007 / 17 years old #205 56.6% (1st Fill Oloroso Sherry Butt Finish) WB 88.23
Benrinnes Adelphi 13 years old 55.5% (1st Fill Oloroso Sherry Hogshead) WB 88.19
Amrut Triparva Triple Distilled 50% (casks as yet unknown) WB 87.19
Mystery whisky WB 88.11

description:

This isn’t just another trip to the market — it’s an immersive culinary adventure that will excite all your senses.

Prepare to witness culinary rockstars in action as they whip up their signature dishes live! Renowned chefs and culinary stars, including MasterChef winners Nadia Lim, Sam Low, and the hilarious Annabelle White, will be sharing their tips, tricks, and insider knowledge in the Chance Voight Cooking Theatre. Stock up on pantry essentials at unbeatable prices, discover hidden gems from local producers, or indulge in luxurious gourmet treats — all while saving big on products you can’t find anywhere else.

Whether you're a seasoned chef or just getting started, The Food Show is your ticket to discovering the best in food, flavour, and fun.

description:
Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ, Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ
It's (nearly) summer so it's time for a BBQ! Come and join us at 43 Kapiti Crescent (St Matthew's Hall) for a BBQ on the lawn. If it's bad weather, we will move into the hall.

All welcome! Dinner will be served from 5pm; we will make dinner, so just bring yourselves!



FAQ

Who is this for? Can I come along?

Yes absolutely, please come, we would love to have you. This dinner is for all the people who live in the beautiful community of Tītahi Bay!

What if I can't make it until a bit later?

That's all good, we will be serving a rolling dinner from 5 to 6.30pm so come whenever suits you. If you can only come a little later than 6.30pm, we will likely have more than enough so come anyway!

Can I bring my kids along?

Yes! In fact, please bring your kids along. We will have some games in the room and some options for crafts on the tables along with the food.

Do I need to bring anything?

Nope! Just yourselves, all are welcome just as you are.

But I really want to bring something to contribute?

If you would like to bring a salad to contribute to the BBQ, feel free to email us at and we can chat! We really just don't want this to be a barrier to anyone coming along.

Can I help?

Yes absolutely, this is a community event so help is always appreciated. It is also a great time to meet some other people. We will have some tasks for set up and also some for packing down and cleaning up. If you are interested in helping, flick us an email at

Will my dietaries be met?

We will make sure there will be options for these dietaries: vegan, gluten free, dairy free, and nut free.

If you have a dietary that isn't on there, feel free to check and flick us an email.

Can I bring my friend(s) along?

Yes, please bring your friends along, especially if they live in Tītahi Bay!

Who is this hosted by?

This idea is hosted by us, the crew who run Tītahi Bay Anglicans, but it is run with the help of our friends around Tītahi Bay. The hope is that this can become a recurring community event where others can join in on hosting this.

This is at a church, will I be preached to?

No, we promise that this isn't a Tupperware party bait and switch. While we definitely are a church, this event is for the Tītahi Bay community as a whole to be able to come eat together and connect.

description:
Vietnamese Pâté Chaud (Bánh Pa-tê Sô), Join Viet Hub NZ for a free Vietnamese cooking workshop celebrating one of Vietnam’s most-loved pastries — Bánh Pa-tê Sô (Vietnamese Pâté Chaud).
In this relaxed, hands-on session, you’ll learn how this golden, flaky pastry is made, explore its key flavours, and hear the cultural stories behind a snack many Vietnamese families grew up with. The workshop is beginner-friendly and designed as a welcoming space to cook, taste, and connect through food.
What makes this workshop special is not just the recipe, but the sharing of culture, memory, and community. Whether you’re new to Vietnamese cuisine or reconnecting with familiar flavours, you’ll leave with new knowledge, warm food, and a deeper appreciation of Vietnamese food culture.
Free to attend | All ingredients provided | Limited spaces – registration required
Come cook with us, meet new people, and enjoy a meaningful cultural experience through food.
This workshop is proudly delivered by Viet Hub NZ, in collaboration with Te Tai Ohinga | Central City Youth Hub, supporting accessible, inclusive spaces for cultural learning and connection ❤️.

Whisky Galore Tasting: Kilchoman 20th Anniversary Tour, Founded in 2005 by Anthony and Kathy Wills, Kilchoman was the first distillery to be built on the island of Islay for over 120 years. In the 20 years since its founding, the Wills family remain driving force behind Kilchoman, keeping the traditions of farm-to-bottle whisky making alive on Islay.

Since their first visit to New Zealand in 2007, the Wills and their whisky have garnered an enthusiastic following, and it is with great pleasure that the team at Whisky Galore announce the 20th Anniversary Tour of Kilchoman, proudly presented by Catherine MacMillan, Brand manager for the distillery.

Join our very special guest Catherine MacMillan, all the way from the Isle of Islay in Scotland, for an evening celebrating the 20th anniversary of Kilchoman. This tasting is a celebration of all things Kilchoman for the past 2 decades, including several of the brand-new, limited edition 20th anniversary whiskies.

description:
Zwanze Day, GP is thrilled to be the exclusive host of Zwanze Day for New Zealand in 2026!

We’ll be tapping Cantillon’s Zwanze beers at the Wild Workshop in Wellington on 25 April, alongside a primo selection of beers from the GP cellar - an event this prestigious calls for the best, and we’re pulling out all the stops.

There are two ways you can join Zwanze Day 2026 at the Wild Workshop:

Get tickets to a guided tasting, hosted by Pete Gillespie and Dave Bell (Wild Workshop Head Brewer).

This session will run for 90 minutes from 1pm. Included in the ticket is a guided tasting of 9 beers (the two 2026 Zwanze beers, a few other Cantillon treats and some of GP’s best from the cellar), food to match and a tour of the Wild Workshop brewery. There are limited spots - get in quick.

Come by the Wild Workshop from 2.30pm for freestyle tasting.

Free entry, open for spontaneous walk-ins (get it). Pay-as-you-go to work your way through the line-up, or get a Zwanze flight, with some delish food to boot.

Zwanze Day happens but once every two years. It’s a global beer event run by renowned Belgian brewery Cantillon; they make a unique, one-off beer especially for the event, and it is tapped simultaneously at select venues across almost two-dozen countries. The Wild Workshop is Cantillon's exclusive partner in New Zealand.

This is the event for lovers of craft beer at its finest.

description:
2025 Taiwan Update Lectures, Taiwan’s Multidimensional Energy Security Challenges
Professor Chyungly Lee
A stable and reliable energy supply is essential for a nation’s economic growth and development. In selecting fuel sources, nowadays almost all countries have taken climate change into account, adopted sensible clean energy transition plans, and designed a schedule to meet the goal of Net Zero. While pursuing a 3-E (energy-economic-environmental) balanced energy supply strategy, Taiwan, lacking indigenous resources, faces unique challenges of supply disruptions from over dependence on energy imports and possible blockade, quarantine, or invasion from Beijing. Any disruption of power supply or surge of energy costs could not only threaten Taiwan’s competitive edge in the global high-tech market but also undermine Taiwan’s internal stability and the nation’s survival. In this talk, Dr. Chyungly Lee will first present fact sheets on Taiwan’s energy status, summarize Taiwan’s current energy strategy, and then discuss dilemmas and vulnerabilities that Taiwan might face in the next few years.
What does Taiwan’s two-level politics tell us?
Professor Alex Tan
This presentation examines Taiwan as a critical case study for understanding the evolving challenges to democracy in the 21st century. Arguing that Taiwan serves as a “canary in the coalmine,” the analysis highlights how the island’s early and persistent political polarization—rooted in identity politics and the legacies of authoritarian rule—prefigures trends now visible in established democracies worldwide. The research explores how deep divisions between the Kuomintang (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), reinforced by institutional and social factors, have led to legislative gridlock, declining trust in political institutions, and a “democratic ceiling” that constrains further democratic development. Taiwan’s precarious geopolitical position, facing constant pressure from the People’s Republic of China, intensifies the dilemma of balancing national security with the protection of civil liberties. The presentation analyzes Taiwan’s innovative responses to disinformation, foreign interference, and public health crises, illustrating both the resilience and fragility of democratic systems under external and internal stress.
Gaming Taiwan: Indigenous Epistemologies in Play
Associate Professor Chia-rong Wu
This research explores how Indigenous knowledge systems in Taiwan are being revitalized through video games. Far from mere entertainment, these games draw on tribal traditions, ancestral stories, and deep connections to the land to create meaningful digital experiences. By blending oral storytelling with interactive gameplay, Taiwanese Indigenous game developers are preserving cultural memory while challenging colonial legacies. Titles like Princess Baleng, Tayal, VuVu, and Gadvia show how games can empower communities and pass down wisdom to younger generations in innovative and engaging ways. Gamers not only play a game but also immerse themselves in digital environments shaped by Indigenous perspectives and values. This study encourages all engaged audiences, including educators and students, to consider video games as powerful tools for cultural resurgence and learning. Focusing on Indigenous Taiwan, it highlights how digital games integrate historical consciousness and interactivity to reimagine the past and future of the island.

50yrs Misuse of Drugs Act: What impact & what next?, The 1975 Misuse of Drugs Act (MoDA) has failed to deliver. Data from the United Nations Office for Drugs and Crime indicates the demand for drugs is greater than ever, while the supply of drugs knows no bounds. The failure and harm caused by the so called 'War on Drugs' is acknowledged globally and witnessed first hand here in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Back in 2011 a comprehensive review of the MoDA conducted by New Zealand Law Commission recommended the MoDA “should be repealed and replaced by a new Act …administered by the Ministry of Health”. HRCA wants to see that recommendation enacted.

New Zealand has a history for bold world leading policy reform: Woman’s Right to Vote; Decriminalisation of Sex Work; National Needle Exchange, Same Sex Marriage and most recently Drug Checking.

This half day Symposium will provide clear evidence why major law reform is necessary and detail the foundations upon which Aotearoa NZ can once again be innovative and lead the way with new drug laws based on evidence, research and experience -providing a safer environment for future generation.

Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa are delighted to have assembled a group of respected independent thinkers with vast experience of drug policy in Aotearoa and beyond, to reflect on the impact of the MoDA and to identify the principles and values needed to underpin new drug laws.

Warren Young: Prof. of Law & Former Deputy President New Zealand Law Commission.
Kirsten Gibson: Chair of Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa and Qualitative Researcher.
Fiona Hutton: Associate Prof. Institute of Criminology, Victoria University of Wellington.
Adam Dorsett: 40 yrs Living/Lived Experience of Prohibited Drug Use, 25yrs in Prison.
Julian Buchanan: Former UNODC Advisor and Criminology Professor.

description:
A Place of Firsts, Globally, citizens assemblies are widely used as an effective way to involve local people in deciding how to address complex issues such as climate change. Despite the repeated failure of standard policy processes, citizens assemblies have only recently made it to New Zealand. Register for this event to find out more about the Porirua Assembly on Climate and its innovations. 
Porirua is known for community-led innovations in governance and delivery, and the Porirua Assembly on Climate continued this tradition by being:
the first climate assembly in New Zealand,  
the first assembly co-designed and organised by an iwi authority and a community group, 
the first assembly process designed to honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi by using a tricameral design,  
the first New Zealand assembly to include children and young people, and 
by creating a new local governance body - the Porirua Community Leaders Forum - that sponsored the Assembly, holds its recommendations and can instigate ongoing community dialogue on local issues. 
Panellists will share learning on the Porirua Assembly’s innovations, talk about why the standard citizens assembly model was modified, dig into what enabled so many firsts and how these worked out in practice. They will reflect on this legacy and possible future impacts. Might these democratic innovations strengthen local democracy elsewhere in Aotearoa New Zealand? 
About the Host and Speakers
Jodi Watene is a Systems Change Lead at Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira Incorporated, was the project manager for the Porirua Assembly and is helping to establish a New Zealand Community of Practice on Indigenous Citizens’ Assemblies.
Makerita Makapelu is a Team Leader for Wesley Community Action in Porirua with a background in performing arts and youth work. She specialises in community-led development and grassroots systems change, and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators.  
Cally O'Neill was a participatory designer of community spaces until 2019 when she shifted her focus towards advocating for Te Tiriti-based deliberative democracy to address the climate and other contemporary crises. She is a founding member of Te Reo O Ngā Tāngata/The People Speak and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators. 
Future Unity, a youth climate group formed during the Assembly process will be represented by Orini Rokx-Taratu and Santino Morehu, who were participants in the Assembly’s youth and community streams.  
Emily Beausoleil is an Associate Professor at Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of Wellington. Her research as a political theorist centres on the dynamics, conditions and challenges of democratic engagement in diverse societies. She is conducting an independent evaluation of the Porirua Assembly process.

This expert roundtable brings together three visiting Ukrainian legal and civil-society practitioners for a focused discussion on the international justice mechanisms being developed in response to Russia’s aggression, and the role that partners such as New Zealand can play in supporting them.
The discussion will explore recent progress on:
the international compensation mechanism for Ukraine, including the Register of Damage and the newly established International Claims Commission;
ongoing efforts to ensure individual accountability for the crime of aggression, including the establishment of a Special Tribunal;
the broader international response grounded in the rules-based international order.
The roundtable forms part of the Oceania Fora on International Justice and Accountability, and is organised in collaboration with the Embassy of Ukraine in Australia, during the Ukrainian delegation’s visit to Australia and New Zealand in February 2026.

Are Prisons Obsolete? A future we make for ourselves., People Against Prisons Aotearoa is an organisation that calls for a transformation in our approach: not just towards what we'd call criminalised behaviour and people, but towards organising the whole of society to support human flourishing.
The carceral system is an industry that does not produce a product, but a world of limited potential. While in the immediate future the cessation of harmful practices such as solitary confinement or abusive 'boot camps' for youth might not require alternatives, abolitionists like Ruth Wilson Gilmore argue that abolition is brought about by building something new. Some alternatives have already been attempted, such as restorative justice, but these programs are routinely discontinued even when they show signs of success. Other alternatives, such as Turuki! Turuki! https://www.beehive.govt.nz/.../2019-12/Turuki%20Turuki.pdf or #CareNotCages, are an imagined future, where education and community involvement transform lives for the better, in contrast to the so-called 'Justice System' limiting them far beyond reason.
Jade Winterburn, PAPA national outreach coordinator and Tāmaki branch secretary, will provide a short presentation followed by Q & A.

Australia, New Zealand, and a post-American Asia, Foreign and defence policy in Australia and New Zealand needs to grapple with the likelihood that the US won't compete with China for regional leadership. Canberra and Wellington thus need to develop strategies that emphasise self-reliance, yet Australia in particular is pursuing ever-closer integration with the United States.
Sam Roggeveen is Program Director of the Lowy Institute’s International Security Program. He is the author of The Echidna Strategy: Australia’s Search for Power and Peace and Our Very Own Brexit: Australia’s Hollow Politics and Where it Could Lead Us. Before joining the Lowy Institute, Sam was a senior strategic analyst in Australia’s peak intelligence agency, the Office of National Assessments, where his work dealt mainly with North Asian strategic affairs, including nuclear strategy and Asian military forces. Sam also worked on arms control policy in Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and as an analyst in the Defence Intelligence Organisation. Sam writes for newspapers and magazines in Australia and around the world, and is a regular commentator on the Lowy Institute’s international magazine, The Interpreter, of which he was the founding editor from 2007 to 2014. Sam also serves as lead editor at the Lowy Institute, and editor of the Lowy Institute Papers.

Book Launch - Isaac Featherston 'Petatone': A Colonial Life, Join us next month to launch Isaac Featherston 'Petatone': A Colonial Life by John E Martin. The book will be launched by Charlotte MacDonald.

Tuesday 7 October, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
All welcome!

'Existing views of Featherston are fragmentary, negative and not very satisfactory. He was the “little Doctor”, a single-minded despot wielding tyrannical power and casting an oppressive shadow. As I began to understand more of his life, I realised that there was little appreciation of a man who had contributed so much.’ —John E.Martin

Isaac Featherston was at the heart of some of the most significant developments in New Zealand from the 1840s colonisation by the New Zealand Company to the abolition of the provinces in 1876. A doctor, newspaper editor and politician, he advocated for the provinces against the domination of central government, while also being primarily responsible for the relocation of the capital from Auckland to Wellington in 1865.

Known amongst Māori as ‘Petatone’ and with a reputation for directness and honesty, he was at the very centre of Pākehā–Māori relations, and in his 1857 official portrait is depicted alongside leading rangatira Te Puni and Wi Tako.

About the author: Dr. John E. Martin has researched and written about New Zealand history since the 1980s, teaching in universities and employed as a historian in the public sector. He was parliamentary historian in the 2000s and 2010s. His publications include rural and labour history, the history of science and engineering, and social and political history. His books include The Forgotten Worker (1990), People, Politics and Power Stations (1991 and 1998), Holding the Balance (1996), The House: New Zealand’s House of Representatives, 1854–2004 (2004), Parliament’s Library (2008), Honouring the Contract (2010), Illuminating Our World (2017), A Colonist’s Gaze (2018) and most recently Empire City: Wellington Becomes the Capital of New Zealand (2022).

About this Event

The next Café des Idées, organised by and , is honoured to host Wendy Nelson and Kevin Hackwell for a captivating discussion on the shared scientific and environmental connections between France and New Zealand in the subantarctic marine world.

Wendy will be talking about important marine collections made on French expeditions of discovery to the NZ subantarctic in the early 1800s that are housed in the Herbarium of the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle in Paris.
Wendy has been collaborating with Professor Line Le Gall (Departement Origines et Evolution) and for two weeks in October they worked to locate and document these important specimens - uncovering answers to some long held questions about the identity of species described over 180 years ago and not found subsequently.
In this talk she will take you into the Herbarium of the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle, Paris - and highlight some of the remarkable treasures housed there.
(This work was supported by funding from the French Embassy in Wellington and the Royal Society of New Zealand Te Apārangi.)
Kevin will talk about the importance of the marine protected areas in the subantarctic and initiatives that have been taken to protect critical habitat for southern seabirds and connections between French and NZ in this critical work.

Wendy Nelson is a botanist and marine biologist, currently Senior Research Fellow Auckland Museum Tāmaki Paenga Hira
Kevin Hackwell is an ecologist, formerly Chief Conservation Advisor for Forest & Bird, a sister organisation to LPO (Ligue pour la Protection des Oiseaux)

China and the Media Landscape in the Pacific, Over the last decade, the People’s Republic of China has sought to deepen its ties with Pacific Island countries. Beijing’s efforts to cultivate influence in the region have included expanding economic, diplomatic, and security ties with Pacific Island nations, as well as expanding China’s footprint in the region’s media landscape. This talk will present the findings of recent research on China’s efforts to shape reporting, media coverage and narratives in the Pacific Islands and put Beijing’s efforts within the context of the region’s rapidly evolving information landscape.
 About the speakers:
Heidi Holz is a Senior Research Scientist at CNA. For close to two decades, her work has focused on PRC strategic communications, propaganda, and influence efforts. She is a graduate of Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service, where she received a master’s degree in security studies and a bachelor’s degree in Chinese and East Asian history.
Genevieve Collins is a research specialist in the China Studies program at CNA, where her research focuses on the behaviour of China’s state-run media and its reactions to US military operations and activities.
 Barbara Dreaver (Discussant) has been the Pacific Reporter for TVNZ 1 News since 2002, breaking stories uncovering social and economic issues affecting Pacific people living in New Zealand and the Pacific Islands. In 2020, she created a two-year training programme through Pacific Cooperation Broadcasting Ltd to support new Pacific journalists across the Pacific region. In the 2024 New Years Honours she was awarded an ONZM for services to investigative journalism and Pacific communities.
 About CNA: CNA is a non-profit, non-governmental research and analysis organization dedicated to providing independent and objective analyses to the U.S. government and the public. This talk will build on previous CNA research on China and the Pacific Islands media landscape which you can find at www.cna.org.

New Zealand’s High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Link has been in service since 1965. It helps keep our electricity system reliable and stable and allows Kiwis to access the lowest-cost electricity across both islands. It’s a critical piece of our national grid. The current HVDC cables were installed in 1991 and have an expected 40-year lifespan, so they need to be replaced by the early 2030s.
As well as replacing the three existing cables and adding a fourth cable, Transpower’s planned renewal programme includes building new cable termination stations at Oteranga Bay and Ōraumoa/Fighting Bay. This work is expected to start in the summer of 2027/2028.
Construction is still some time away, but we want to share our plans with communities near our sites and hear from them about how we can best understand and manage possible impacts.
Come along to Makara Community Hall on Sunday May 3, 10am-2pm.
Grab a coffee and cookie and meet some of the Transpower team
Learn more about the thinking and planning behind the HVDC Link renewal work
Quiz us on HVDC history (our specialist topic!)
Learn how we will update you on our plans
Bring your questions, feedback and any concerns
We’d love to hear from as many local voices as we can. Please share widely with whānau, friends and local organisations.

Connected Theatres or Fractured World? Emerging Threats and Collective Responses Across the Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific, Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 it has become clear that threats in the Euro-Atlantic region and the Indo-Pacific are profoundly inter-connected. North Korean troops and weapons have helped Russia’s war effort and Chinese technologies have sustained its military industrial base. Ships registered in the Pacific have been part of Russia’s sanctions-busting ‘shadow fleet’ and implicated in cable-cutting activities in the Baltic Sea. Conversely, Russia has transferred advanced weapons technologies to North Korea, and lessons from the war in Ukraine have implications for Indo-Pacific flashpoints, including across the Taiwan Strait. But if cross-theatre links are clear, forging collective responses has become much more complicated. The recent US National Defence Strategy points to a more limited US role in Europe and expectations that in the Indo-Pacific allies and partners will have to do more. International order is in flux. What does all this mean for New Zealand, for our region, for partners, and for global security?
