description:
Wellington Book Launch | Hoods Landing by Laura Vincent, Join Āporo Press at Unity Books Wellington on Halloween, 31 October, to celebrate the debut novel by Laura Vincent.
Friday 31 October, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
All welcome!
Rita considered the dead. Shut her eyes. Rolled their names around her brain. Stacked each person in order like folded laundry, warm and crisp from the sun. She wondered how her name would sound amongst them.
In the rural reaches of Auckland, the women of the eclectic Gordon family gather for Christmas. They may push each other’s buttons, but know precisely when to offer tea (or a tipple). Rita, the 50-year-old baby of the family, is planning to tell them she has cancer. Drifting between past and present, she considers the lives of women in their community and reckons with what it all means for her future and her family.
Featuring elderly lesbians, twins who aren’t twins, and several dogs named Roger, Hoods Landing is about shoddy pasts, ambiguous futures and the imperfect bonds that tie family together.
About the author:
Laura Vincent (Ngāti Māhanga, Ngāpuhi) is an author whose work spans fiction, poetry and food writing. She has written the food blog hungryandfrozen.com since 2007, and her debut cookbook was published by Penguin Random House in 2013. Laura’s poetry has appeared in anthologies published by Āporo Press, Auckland University Press and Muswell Press, and she completed her Master of Creative Writing at Auckland University of Technology in 2022. Born in Waiuku, Laura currently lives in Tāmaki Makaurau. Hoods Landing is her first novel.

description:
YEPN Wellington - Sustainable Aviation Fuel: A Strategic Approach, The Young Energy Professionals Network is pleased to invite you to our next Wellington event, proudly hosted by Z Energy at their waterfront offices.
This event will feature a panel discussion on one of the toughest – and most important – challenges in the energy transition: decarbonising aviation through Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)*.
Aviation is one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonise and by 2050, it could contribute more than a third of Aotearoa New Zealand’s total emissions. Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is emerging as a critical decarbonisation tool, and momentum is building both locally and globally.
In this session, we’ll bring together voices from across the aviation ecosystem – industry leaders, suppliers and customers – to explore how SAF is being adopted, scaled and supported in Aotearoa and overseas. From feedstocks and policy settings to operational realities and investment signals, we’ll unpack what’s driving demand, what barriers remain, and where the biggest opportunities lie.
Whether you're curious about the technology, the economics, or the practicalities of adoption, this is your chance to take a deep dive into an important fuel in the energy transition.
Panelists include:
Julian Hughes, GM Supply, Z Energy
Billie Moore, Chief Executive, NZ Airports Association
Peter van Cingel, Business Development Manager, Channel Infrastructure NZ

Drinks and nibbles provided
Spaces are limited — register below to secure your spot.
* 'Sustainable Aviation Fuel' is an industry term used to describe fuels manufactured using waste and purpose grown feedstocks, including used cooking oil (UCO), tallow and canola oil, and can provide carbon emissions reductions on a life cycle basis.

description:
Expressive Watercolour, Watercolour is special because of the fluid properties that produce spontaneous and unique results. The inability to anticipate exactly what the paint will do makes watercolour an exciting medium to work with.

In this course we will learn to set the conditions for surprising and beautiful accidents to occur on the page. By incorporating these looser abstract elements into representational paintings we can convey heightened emotions in our work.

Throughout the term we will cover the following:

- The wet into wet technique to achieve one of a kind paint interactions.
- Learn about transparent colour mixing to create luminosity in your paintings.
- Use marbling to find organic shapes and patterns.
- Study the relationship between line and colour and the different
- Ways they can be combined to find a personal style.
- Experiment with composition through collage.

Each class we will look at examples of historic and contemporary painting, and discuss how to selectively incorporate references into your work. Over the term you will build up a visual style and body of work.

Whether you’re new to watercolour or looking to expand your range, this course offers an opportunity to explore the expressive potential of watercolour.

Basic materials included. Students must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

description:
Scottish Country Dancing, Scottish Country Dancing
Why do Scottish Country Dancing? Great music and amazing ‘brain gym’ for body and mind! Scottish Country Dancing is a very social form of dancing, danced in "sets" usually with four "couples" - unlike Highland Dancing which is usually solo dancing. Have fun and meet new people, while getting fit!
It’s suitable for all levels of fitness, and is a great way of meeting and socialising with new people. Scottish country dancing is a common pastime for thousands of dancers in many countries, whether you’re in Japan, Germany, the US or Scotland itself.
Wear soft flat shoes and loose clothing and bring a bottle of water. No partner is needed – we change partners for every dance!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Name and perform to beginner level the five major steps of Scottish Country Dancing
• Name and perform ten simple formations
• Participate in five simple Scottish Country dances, in strathspey (slow) and reel/jig (fast) tempo
• Clap rhythm to reel, jig and strathspey tempo
• Have the confidence and skills to join a club to progress your social dancing 
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk].

description:
Sip & Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // The Bond Store Distillery, Sip & Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // The Bond Store Distillery
Come and experience this unique Sip & Kintsugi workshop at the lovely Bond Store Distillery. You will get a gin tasting tray on arrival with three different gins with tonic. And why not come a little earlier and grab a bite to eat beforehand. (Must be 18years +)

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Friday 26th June - 5:30pm - 7:30pm


Ema has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

description:
The World of Ikebana - Tension and the Beauty of Space, Have you ever heard of Ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arrangement?

With a history spanning over 1,400 years, Ikebana is far more than decorative floral design. It is a refined art form that expresses space, balance, seasonality, and life itself. Today, Ikebana is internationally recognised and practiced by enthusiasts around the world.

Through careful techniques such as proper water preparation and pruning, flowers can be enjoyed for weeks, subtly changing their appearance over time.
This event invites you to explore the history, philosophy, and aesthetics of Ikebana, followed by a hands-on workshop where you can experience the art firsthand.
By engaging with flowers, space, and silence, participants are encouraged to sense the changing seasons and reflect on the essence of life.

Part I: Lecture & Demonstration, Q&A
Part II: Workshop

In this hands-on session, you will learn how to:



• Prepare and season a traditional crab-based broth

• Work with thick tapioca or rice noodles

• Balance flavours and textures with crab meat and fresh herbs

• Present the dish beautifully, Vietnamese style



Bánh Canh Cua is a beloved Southern Vietnamese dish, often enjoyed as a nourishing family meal. Its naturally thick broth and delicate sweetness from crab make it perfect for cooler days.



Participants will cook together, share stories, and enjoy tasting the finished bowl as a group.



To help keep these classes sustainable and support ongoing community activities, there will be an additional $10 contribution per class. This supports:



• Facilitator preparation and effort

• Administration and coordination

This workshop continues our collaboration with I Love Viet Food and is made possible thanks to the generous support of:



• Hutt City Council

description:
5 days Figure Sculpting workshop with model, 5 days Figure Sculpting workshop with model
The immediacy of the model’s presence encourages close observation and instinctive decision-making leading to work that is expressive and real. This hands-on interaction brings a sense of movement and authenticity that’s hard to achieve otherwise.

The sculpting process typically starts by analyzing the model’s proportions and pose. A wire armature is built to support the structure and clay is gradually applied to develop the form to a one-third life size 750mm tall figure. From there the artist refines the shapes focusing on anatomical accuracy and expressive detail that give the sculpture its final character.

With nearly 30 years of experience in traditional sculpture and the film industry Javier is not just a sculptor — he’s a mentor. Trained in classical techniques he studied fine arts and took anatomy courses at medical school developing a rare combination of artistic and anatomical knowledge. He spent over five years at the world-renowned Weta Workshop contributing to major films and exhibitions and has worked across materials scales and digital technologies.

Material is included in the price.
Armature is supplied during the workshop.
You can buy our tools during the workshop if you like.

description:
British and Irish Film Festival - Beat the Lotto, - OFFICIAL SELECTION: Dublin International Film Festival 2025 -

Beat the Lotto is a rip-roaring tale about the mathematician who, along with a ragtag syndicate, plotted to fix Ireland’s National Lottery in 1992, captivating the nation and sparking rabid debate.

In Ireland, the public became obsessed when the National Lottery arrived, none more so than mathematician and avid stamp-collector Stefan Klincewicz. Using mathematical analysis, he reckoned the system could be beaten if he could just gather enough people to form a syndicate to buy every single ticket combination – and front up all the cash, of course.

Director Ross Whitaker fashions this unbelievable true story into a gripping thriller, mirroring the tension felt by the public as the lottery authorities caught wind of the plan.

With insightful interviews and fantastic archival footage, Beat the Lotto is a look back at Ireland in the 1990s and a compelling tale of one man’s attempt to outsmart the system.
Director
Ross Whitaker

description:
French Film Festival - Leave One Day, Making waves in 2025 as the first-ever debut feature selected to open the Cannes Film Festival, Amélie Bonnin’s joyously entertaining musical romance stars break-out singer/songwriter Juliette Armanet as a talented Parisian chef forced to reconnect with her small-town upbringing during an unexpected trip home.
Cécile (Armanet) – a fan-favourite Top Chef winner – is about to finally realise her dream and open her own restaurant when her father, the cook at a small rural truck stop, falls unwell.

Cécile must deal with a return to her roots that is more complicated than she imagined; when she runs into her teenage first love (César Award-winner Bastien Bouillon), old memories and sensations resurface... and then her fiancé, who senses something’s wrong, shows up.
Evocatively depicting regional France and the complications of family life with tenderness and wit, Leave One Day interweaves music naturally into the story, blending several classics with more recent hits by artists such as Stromae and Céline Dion.

Armanet, herself one of France’s most popular contemporary artists, performed John Lennon’s “Imagine” during the Paris Olympic Games’ opening ceremony and proves to be a shining discovery, in this warm-hearted and completely endearing gem.

Directed by Rebecca Tansley, TENOR: My Name Is Pati follows Pene’s journey alongside his brother Amitai — also a rising opera star — from their humble beginnings in the South Pacific to the world’s greatest opera houses.
Weaving intimate family archive footage with behind-the-scenes moments and soaring performances, this music-rich documentary blends humour and heart to reveal how family, cultural pride, and determination can carry an unlikely dream to the world stage.

Let the good times ROLL! The screening sensation known as The Big Bike Film Night is back in '26 for your bike films fix!!!

Two screenings
Tuesday 24th March | 6:00pm, and 6:15pm


What's it all about??? The Big Bike Film Night is on a mission- bringing the best cycling short films from around the world together for you.

Showcasing 2.5 hours of riveting bike films that have everything a cycle-centric audience could want - action, drama, humour, and plenty of inspiration; the evening is unashamedly and utterly, utterly, utterly designed and devised to delight the two-wheel devotee!

Our Promo Trailer
https://bit.ly/Big_Bike_Film_Night_2026_Promo_Trailer

The 2026 treasure chest of films includes:
• a dazzling mountain bike ride exploring the breathtaking landscapes of Norway, embracing the magic of the midnight sun
• a life-changing experience for two adventurous women as they embark to cycle to all the ski-fields in New Zealand in one gigantic attempt
• an inspiring film that captures the wettest, most miserable riding conditions imaginable
• a film that playfully delves into the world of those taking cycling to new heights - celebrating fun, silliness, and creativity that comes with pushing boundaries on two wheels
• a compelling story about perseverance, showcasing the challenges and triumphs of navigating daily life following a life-altering injury, and how adaptive design has transformed and enriched the journey forward
• a moving movie that follows a father and son’s journey as they take on one of life’s most meaningful milestones- riding a bike together as a family
• a bold and uplifting story of an adventure activist, attempting to break the 24-hour Guinness World Record in downhill mountain biking- all to raise funds for reforesting foothills around Queenstown, New Zealand. Her relentless pursuit not only pushes the limits of endurance but also becomes a powerful symbol of resilience and environmental commitment
• and crowning the night off… we all love an underdog tale. This charming, funny, heartfelt film inspires us to believe that we all have the capacity to be unlikely heroes in our own stories. The audience is transported back to the nostalgic 1990s, to the slopes of the punishing Mont Ventoux, in Southern France, to witness the drama of a battle between two giants
ALL in the mix!

These short films are a great reminder of why we love to ride our bike; with stories that captivate us, stories that make us think, and most importantly of all- inspiring us to get out and ride. All celebrate the fun, adventure, and joy that cycling enables.

11 November Whisky Tasting, Whisky Tasting: 11 November 2025
Hosted by Matt Mueller
On November 11, we will dive into the penultimate whisky tasting of the year: New Zealand whiskies!
New Zealand has a long and complex history with single malts, stretching all the way back to the earliest Scottish settlers in the 1830's.  Government regulations shut that down in the 1870's, however, it became revitablsed in the 1970's at the Willowbank Distillery in Dunedin.  Willowbank  shut down in 1997, but we have an early 1990's bottle to take a look at!
The New Zealand single malt industry started growing again in the mid-2000's and now has a thriving craft whisky scene on both islands.
In addition to the older style of whisky, we'll sample some contemporary whiskies from the likes of 8 Wired, Pokeno and a few others...
Please join me at the Seatoun Clubhouse at 7:30pm on November 11th, for this special tasting.  $60 per seat.  See you then,
Matt

Founded by The Ear Nurses at Crystal Clear Ears in partnership with the Ear Health Education CPD Portal, Ear Health Australia (EHA) is dedicated to advancing excellence in ear health and fostering professional growth across Australasia.

Our presenters are highly respected leaders in aural health nursing and education.

description:
Food is My Medicine: A Transformative Evening with Sri Ganesh, Food is My Medicine: A Transformative Evening with Sri Ganesh
Join Sri Ganesh for an inspiring Ayurveda talk on how food & senses shape health. Learn 6 tastes, conscious eating, balancing your dominant

About this Event



Food is My Medicine: A Transformative Evening with Sri Ganesh

What you feed your body and mind today shapes your health tomorrow.
Join us for an inspiring and eye-opening lecture with renowned Ayurvedic teacher and bestselling author Sri Ganesh, as he guides us through the powerful connection between physical and mental food—and how they shape our well-being.
In this talk, you’ll discover:
The two types of food we consume: what we eat with our mouths, and what we absorb through our senses.
How to make choices that support both body and mind—using Ayurveda’s six tastes as your guide.
Practical tools to shop wisely, cook from the heart, and eat consciously.
How to align your food and lifestyle with your presently dominant element (PDE) to prevent or heal imbalances at any age.
Whether you’re curious about Ayurveda, seeking to improve your health, or looking to deepen your relationship with food—this lecture will leave you empowered, informed, and inspired.
Sri Ganesh is the author of nine books, including the cookbooks 'Food is my medicine' and 'Food from my village’.




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!



Meet Your Host: Sri Ganesh

Sri Ganesh, the founder of Vaidya’s Ayurveda Village in Kerala, India, is an internationally recognised Ayurveda practitioner, inspirational speaker, and the author of eight widely read health books published in nine languages across the United States, Europe, and India.
Born into a traditional family in South India, Sri Ganesh began his education in Ayurveda in the early years of his life with his grandmother, a well-respected Ayurveda practitioner and poison therapist in their village. He later expanded his knowledge in the subjects of Mana-shastra (psychology), Vedanta (philosophy), Dhyana (meditation), Kalari Marma Chikitsa (Kerala martial art therapy), and Yoga Chikitsa (yoga therapy) through traditional schools in South Indian villages known as gurukulams. Sri Ganesh also holds a bachelor’s degree from Mahatma Gandhi University and a master’s degree in Human Resource Development (HRD).
Drawing on his traditional knowledge and over two decades of experience working as an Ayurveda practitioner around the world, Sri Ganesh has travelled extensively throughout Europe and the United States as an ambassador of Ayurveda, sharing his ancestors’ wisdom through talks, columns, and books. Over the years, Ganesh has delivered hundreds of inspirational talks and has written eight books in the field of health, which have been translated and published in Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Norway, the Netherlands, the United States, India, and Brazil.

Hailing from Portland Oregon, The Decemberists is an indie-alt folk rock band that write epic songs and have 9 studio albums to their credit. They are renowned for their musical style and unique storytelling with many song lyrics based on historical incidents and folklore. Perhaps drawing musical influence from the likes of The Beatles, Tom Waits, REM, Morrisey, their songs are exquisitely constructed and effortlessly combine folk-rock with elements of pop creating the infectious sound that is The Decemberists.
And who is BANDIT QUEEN? Experienced Christchurch based musos - Tim Kent (vocals, acoustic guitar); Justin 'Rusty' White (lead guitar); Jo-Anne Davern Fuller (vocals, keyboard); Chiara Lowe (violin, vocals); Adam Lowe (bass); Mark Newburn (drums, percussion).
The members of BANDIT QUEEN are passionate about this project and invite you to come experience and enjoy the eclectic music of USA indie-rock band THE DECEMBERISTS.

description:
CHAT PILE (USA) & BEASTWARS, Sludgy noise superstars CHAT PILE have announced their first ever Australia & New Zealand tour for June 2026. Fusing elements of post-punk, nu metal, grunge, they have earned a cult following for their eclectic take on what they simply deem ‘noise rock.’ 
Formed in 2019, the band took their name from piles of chat, byproducts of mining which are commonly found throughout northeast Oklahoma. Their adopted stage names Raygun Busch, Luther Manhole, Stin and Cap’n Ron were conjured as a way of avoiding identification from previous employers.
Following the band’s self-released debut ‘This Dungeon Earth’, they were signed to The Flenser in 2020 and released their debut album ‘God’s Country’. The album received broad acclaim, including ‘Best New Music’ on Pitchfork. 
Their second full-length record ‘Cool World’ was releasing in 2024. They went on to headline Roadburn Festival 2025 and tour extensively, earning a reputation for an incendiary live show.
Joining Chat Pile in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington is Kiwi sludge metal band BEASTWARS. The veteran group originally formed in the late 1980s and have abided by one steadfast maxim ever since: obey the riff. It’s time. 
Dig into Chat Pile this June.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
CMNZ Series From Scratch, New Zealand’s oldest and most avant-garde chamber music ensemble, From Scratch, has been performing nationally and internationally since 1974, principally under the leadership of sound and intermedia artist Phil Dadson.

From Scratch have developed an original and innovative sound/performance style that includes large sculptural invented instruments (primarily percussion), and innovative hocket-style rhythms – where the performers’ individual parts interlock to create complex rhythmic and melodic structures.

The current collective core-group consists of Adrian Croucher, Shane Currey, Phil Dadson, Darryn Harkness and Chris O'Connor.

description:
CMNZ Series: Four Last Songs - Wellington, CMNZ Series: Four Last Songs - Wellington
This October, Chamber Music New Zealand is proud to tour Aotearoa's own NZTrio (Amalia Hall - violin, Somi Kim - piano, Matthias Balzat - cello) and Australian soprano Emma Pearson in Four Last Songs, a concert reflecting on the nature of goodbyes, endings, and renewals.

Named for Strauss' Four Last Songs which he wrote towards the end of his life — now arranged for piano trio and soprano — the songs reflect on the serene acceptance of mortality and a closeness with nature.

The concert also features Salina Fisher's Kintsugi, about the Japanese art of putting broken ceramics back together with gold and celebrating the beauty of a life not unmarred by difficulty, but made more beautiful by the resilience of overcoming hardship.

PROGRAMME

🎶 Elena Kats-Chernin | The Spirit and the Maiden
🎶 Salina Fisher | Kintsugi
🎶 Amy Beach | 2 Songs Op. 100 A Mirage and Stella Viatoris
🎶 Sergei Rachmaninoff | Vocalise
🎶 Richard Strauss (arr. Salina Fisher) | Four Last Songs (Vier letzte Lieder) TrV 296

Kiwi blues legend brings the special sauce!

Darren Watson –This Here Guitar Tour ‘26 - Darren is heading back to The Shed after two sold out shows late last year! Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm. Limited seats will sell out fast.

From leading the iconic Chicago Smoke Shop to working alongside greats like Dr.John, Keb Mo, Billy Boy Arnold, and Tony Joe White, Darren Watson has been serving up the finest cuts of New Zealand blues music for decades.

His latest release, Darren Watson Sings John Hiatt, recently simmered its way up to #3 on the Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart.

Watson is hitting the road again to deliver his trademark powerful vocals, astonishing yet understated guitar playing, and soulful,"pin-drop" intensity live.

Don’t miss this tasty-serving of world-class blues and Americana.

What folks say:

“If Ry Cooder had a long-lost New Zealand cousin, it would be Darren Watson.”
Tami Neilson (Kiwi country/blues legend)

“It’s not easy writing catchy tunes that carry a message, but Darren pulls it off easily, singing in his big, soulful voice: ‘...you can hold folks up, you can knock folksdown, it matters what we do and what we say.’ Right on!”
Rick Holmstrom (Mavis Staples Band)

“... outstanding by any measure.”
Downbeat Magazine (USA)

The 51 dates across Australia, Aotearoa, Europe & UK will be Freddy’s first shows following the sudden death of founding band member Chris ‘MU’ Faiumu. The band is united in its decision to continue with this long-planned tour.
Lead singer Dallas Tamaira says, ‘It’s important for us to honour the intentions we had with MU and playing
this album live is part of that.’
Based On A True Story was independently released in 2005, an album of 10 fresh slices of future funk, with surprises, fakes & freaky sidesteps. In a historic run, the album became Aotearoa’s Longest-Charting Album with 111 weeks in the Top 40, won eight NZ Music Awards and took out Giles Peterson’s Worldwide Music
Awards in the UK.
‘This was the band’s first full length studio album and its success was the springboard for what has been an incredible journey together’, explains saxophonist Scott Towers. ‘We want to pay tribute to the music, to MU and the band he established. And, of course, to play to our fans around the world who have supported us through everything.’

⏰ Pre-sale starts Thur 30 Oct at 11am (local)
⏰ General tickets go on sale Fri 31 Oct at 11am (local)
⚡️ Sign up for pre-sale access
PRE-SALE: https://bit.ly/MM26_ps_DNU

Handsome Tours are proud to present Matt Maltese on his highly anticipated return to Australia + New Zealand this March!
The tour follows the release of his sixth studio album Hers – his most insular and intimate record yet, and his first fully self-produced effort since his acclaimed 2019 LP Krystal.
Existing in a twilight world, Hers pairs heartfelt songwriting and dry witticism with the gentle quiver of strings, a flourish of woodwind and the sound of a creaking old piano. It captures Maltese at his most personal, trading irony for honesty and humour for vulnerability.

Much like kindred spirits Randy Newman and Father John Misty, beneath Maltese’s sumptuous melodies and classic pop craftsmanship there’s always a lyric that stops you in your tracks – sometimes breaking your heart, sometimes making you laugh. Across the album’s eleven tracks, Maltese’s trademark wit is still present but wielded with restraint, often emerging through self-deprecation and quiet revelation.

Having first established himself in 2018 with his debut Bad Contestant, Maltese has since evolved into one of the UK’s finest young songwriters. The albums that followed cemented his reputation for transforming the mundane into something dream-like, his piano harmonies, playful lyricism and quintessentially British wit resonating around the world.

In late 2024, Maltese embarked on a headline tour across Asia, Australia and New Zealand, following sold-out runs through the US, Europe and the UK – including his biggest performances to date at The Wiltern in Los Angeles and London’s Electric Brixton. With Hers, he now steps into an even bigger chapter: playing to larger rooms than ever before and connecting with an audience that continues to grow from Sydney to São Paulo, Jakarta to Tokyo.

Audiences can expect an enchanting live experience that blends Maltese’s new material with an favourites spanning his six-album catalogue – poetic, wry, and unashamedly human.

description:
NZTrio presents Hypnotique, Described as a “national treasure” and “New Zealand’s most indispensable ensemble”, NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists, every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

Hypnotique presents a diverse array of works that challenges expectations of traditional chamber music. A whirlwind of motion typifies NZ composer Lyell Cresswell's virtuosic Moto Perpetuo, ahead of Fauré's Piano Trio in D minor with lyrical elegance and lush harmonic textures, contrasting with the percussive and electronic influences in Le Boeuf's jazz-adjacent Obliquely Wrecked. Australian composer Elena Kats-Chernin pays homage to Haydn, blending classical and contemporary styles in Calliope Dreaming, then finally, the full Romantic immersion of Schönberg's Verklärte Nacht is structured around the five stanzas of a poem; deeply transcendent and utterly beautiful.

The Programme (2 hours including 20min interval)

Lyell Cresswell (NZ) - Moto perpetuo
Gabriel Fauré - Piano Trio in D minor, Op. 120
Pascal Le Boeuf - Obliquely Wrecked
Elena Kats-Chernin - Calliope Dreaming

The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

description:
Nonconnah (USA) / 1/3 Octave Band, Nonconnah is an experimental music collective based in Memphis, Tennessee, headed by the husband-and-wife duo of Zachary Corsa and Denny Wilkerson Corsa.
Nonconnah creates haunting soundscapes and collages, often using antique or unusual instrumentation and obsolete recording technology to draw on themes of memory and the past, the supernatural, and the liminal spaces where the man-made and natural worlds meet.
Releases such as 2021's Songs for and About Ghosts are filled with warped lo-fi guitars, field recordings, grainy samples, and acoustic instrumentation, arranged into dreamlike sequences. The Corsas draw on a wide range of sonic influences, from shoegaze and post-rock to dark ambient to recurring motifs of old time/Appalachian mountain music.
A highly collaborative effort, Nonconnah has collaborated with past and present members of bands like Deerhoof, Swans, Earth, Broken Social Scene, Arcade Fire, A Silver Mt. Zion and many more.

description:
Rhian Sheehan & Arli Liberman - Traces Album Release Tour, Loop are proud to announce that acclaimed New Zealand musicians, composers and producers Rhian Sheehan and Arli Liberman will bring their collaborative album Traces to life for the first time ever, with a special three-show tour this November.

The tour will see the pair perform the album in its entirety at a series of intimate shows in Auckland, Wellington & Christchurch. These shows will see them accompanied by Ed Zuccollo and Riki Pirihi aka Riki Gooch (TrinityRoots, Orchestra Of Spheres) to bring the album to the stage.

This tour marks the long-awaited debut live performance of Traces, an instrumental journey blending electronic, ambient and post-rock soundscapes to create a world unlike anything else — described by filmmaker Sam Kelly as “an ethereal journey through dark and moody worlds.”

For the first time, audiences will be able to experience this collaboration in a live setting. With both artists renowned for their powerful, emotive performances and their ability to craft immersive sound journeys, these shows promise to be as visually striking as they are sonically transporting. Live performances from both Sheehan and Liberman are a rare treat, and this will be only the second-time ever both musicians will be performing together live.

Each show will see Sheehan and Liberman joined by two collaborators on stage to help bring the worlds created in Traces to life. Ed Zuccollo will bring his trademark synth-wizardry to the stage, as he did across a number of tracks on the album. His trademark sound has seen him perform with the likes of Troy Kingi, Kita, The Black Seeds and more, in addition to his own solo work as Zuke. Riki Pirihi aka Riki Gooch is one of NZ’s most celebrated musicians for his work with TrinityRoots, Fat Freddy’s Drop, Cave Circles, and countless others.

The four musicians will combine to perform Traces live, with the second half of the show featuring all four musicians collaborating live on stage with tracks from each artist’s individual catalogues.

These shows will also feature the stunning visuals created for the project by Dunedin-based visual artist Sam Caldwell, which are featured across the album cover and music videos. The Traces live experience will be a richly layered audio and visual feast, unlike anything either artist has performed before..

Tickets go on sale Thursday September 25. Audiences are encouraged to secure theirs early — with only three shows nationwide, these performances promise to be rare, unforgettable events. Presented by Loop, thanks to Manuka Phuel.

About this Event

SOLOS 2025

22 original pieces of theatre! A whooping 6 hrs of new performance work!
Worlds range and collide in hospital waiting rooms, lonesome dreamscapes, loving tributes, acid-jazz ranting, monstrous dinner parties, undercover spy agencies and much, much more. These are the imaginings of a new and powerful generation of artists, full of heart, humour, politics and courage.

Solos is an investigation of performance and storytelling by the first year Acting cohort and Arts Management tauira from 1st, 2nd and 3rd year. Facilitated by experienced artists, Acting tauira are encouraged to follow their interests and supported to create a short solo performance of their own devising. Devising solo work allows actors to have autonomy over body and story, and there no restrictions on the form or content of their creations. BPAM tauira grow their skills in Production Management, Stage Management, Sound and Lighting Design, and Technical Operation, inside a devising process. This collaboration allows these young artists to experiment and translate ideas into performance and storytelling, strengthen their working relationships, and make the kind of work they want to see in the world.

This year solos is facilitated by Matu Ngaropo, Sean Rivera, Anya Tate-Manning, Theresa Hanaray and Alex Fisher, with support from Makini Calliste-Woollard, Erina Daniels, Selena Pirika, Emele Ugavale and Salesi Le’ota.

Solos have a long tradition at Toi Whakaari and many graduates have gone on create longer solo works that tour the world, such as Jacob Rajan, Chris Parker and Kristyl Neho.

Each solos group contains four or five 15 minute pieces, allowing audiences to enjoy range of work and styles - a smorgasbord of theatre sure to delight!

description:
Third Chapter, 
D, Muss & JLaw is a jazz trio that embodies the spirit of creative rebellion, their music a potent fusion of genre-bending experimentation and emotional intensity. Comprised of pianist James 'Muss' Illingworth, drummer Darren 'D' Mathiassen, and bassist Johnny 'JLaw' Lawrence, this trio has forged a unique sound that defies categorization. Soundscapes oscillate between heavy jazz and thumping hip-hop beats, soaring to emotionally powerful improvisations and dissolving into moments of sublime euphoria.
Their compositions are a testament to their collective creativity, weaving together intricate polyrhythms, hypnotic melodies, and explosive improvisations that conjure the raw energy of a live performance. Illingworth's piano playing is a masterclass in dynamic range, shifting seamlessly from delicate nuance to thunderous crescendo, often augmented by his deft use of synthesizers and electronic textures. Mathiassen's drumming is a force of nature, his polyrhythmic wizardry propelling the music forward with unstoppable momentum, while Lawrence's bass lines provide the foundation, his earth-shaking tones anchoring the trio's sonic explorations.
The trio's connection is palpable, their synergy born of years of collaboration and experimentation. They've worked with some of the biggest names in music, from Shapeshifter to Bliss n Eso to Louis Baker to Allen Stone, and their experience has honed their craft, allowing them to push the boundaries of jazz and beyond.
When D, Muss & JLaw takes the stage, the energy is electric. Their performances are a testament to their deep connection, their music a living, breathing entity that evolves and adapts in the moment. They're not just playing notes - they're conjuring emotions, telling stories, and transporting their audience to a realm of sonic wonder. This is their Third Chapter.

description:
Vegyn Wellington, Vegyn Wellington
Sprawling with obtuse bass lines, sharp digital peaks and asymmetrical drum machines, Vegyn’s music doesn’t walk a straight line so much as trip over itself beautifully.

The London-born producer, artist, DJ and label head returns to Australia and New Zealand this October for a rare run of headline shows, supported by NYC producer amr*.

Sign up to our presale here to gain first access to tickets on Wednesday 27th August

---> http://go.astralpeople.com/vegyn-ps


Across everything he touches - from surreal club sets to production work for Travis Scott, JPEGMafia and Frank Ocean - Joseph Thornalley makes music that’s hard to pin down and harder to forget. His productions are jagged and abstract, built from negative space, ambient haze and rhythms that never quite resolve. There’s hip hop in the DNA, but it never plays by the rules, always veering towards something stranger, softer, rawer.

Through his label PLZ Make It Ruins, Vegyn has built an entire world. His 2019 debut Only Diamonds Cut Diamonds felt like a manifesto; the 71-track Text While Driving If You Want To Meet God! followed as a chaotic, genre-agnostic statement of intent. Since then, he’s ventured further leftfield, releasing The Head Hurts but the Heart Knows the Truth under the alias Headache, followed by the 2024 masterpiece The Road to Hell Is Paved with Good Intention, and the unexpected arrival of Blue Moon Safari - an output that feels made more for himself than for any audience. Dreamlike, disjointed and deeply personal.

As a DJ, Vegyn shifts between industrial breaks, ambient drift and warped club memories. This October, he returns to Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Wellington and Auckland - a rare chance to slip through the cracks and step inside his world.

description:
Wilson Blackley The Remain Tour with Oscar LaDell, Wilson Blackley The Remain Tour with Oscar LaDell
Wilson Blackley The Remain Tour with Oscar LaDell.

Wilson Blackley is an Australian multi-instrumentalist and producer currently based in Melbourne.

Born and raised in Poowong (Victoria), Wilson was surrounded by music from an early age. At just 2 years old he started playing the drums along to his mother’s music collection consisting of old soul, funk and r&b from the 60’s and 70’s. He started learning the guitar as soon as he could, and had the habit of making anything he could get his hands on into an instrument. Growing up far from the city instilled a strong sense of curiosity and work ethic in him from a young age, leading him to produce his first batch of demos in his teenage years. A stand-out among these demos was the song ‘Home’

‘Home’ found its way to Sam Teskey (The Teskey Brothers) who would go on to co-produce the song alongside Wilson when he was just 18.

Following the release of ‘Home’, he went on to sell out The Gasometer and play a string of festival slots alongside a variety of artists including The Teskey Brothers and Boy and Bear.

At this time, Wilson moved to St Kilda and in the heart of Melbourne began collaborating with Sensible J (Sampa The Great, Remi, Immy Owusu) on his debut EP ‘Material Plane P1’ which was released to critical acclaim in August 2022. After that, he co-produced Oscar LaDell’s EP ‘No Blue’ and subsequently embarked on a co-headline tour of Aotearoa and Australia with LaDell. After a three year break from releasing music, Wilson Blackley will return with his new song ‘Wired’ that bridges the sonics from his first EP with what's to come.

Also appearing Oscar LaDell hot off a US tour.

Spiritual Retreat (3 Day Event) Sorry for any inconvenience: CANCELLED, Welcome and Thank you for your interest in the Energy & Beyond: Spiritual Retreat.

This weekend with accommodation is created as a fun-filled weekend of learning with like-minded people.

Ari and Tiffany will be guiding you through a full weekend of enhancing your spiritual awareness, learning new skills, and honing the ones you already have. All this in a SAFE, RESPECTFUL AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT.

This is a weekend of full immersive interaction with spirit, your soul and heart. Bring comfortable clothes, rain jacket, yoga mat, walking shoes for wet conditions and an open mind for learning.

All bedding and towels are provided. Each room has a bathroom across the corridor, shared between two. Breakfast, morning tea and dinners are all provided. On the menu we have vegetarian curry and soups for dinners, porridge for breakfast. If you would prefer something different you are welcome to use the kitchen facilities. We also ask you to bring your favourite snacks and preferred lunches, which can be stored in fridges if need be. If you have any special dietary requirements please let us know. We will endeavour to do our best however there may well be cross contamination that we are unaware of.

We would appreciate you taking this opportunity to connect without technology by leaving your phone in your room.

Arrival time is Friday 5th June 12:30pm onwards. Departure time is Monday 8th June 2pm. A deposit will be required for confirmation of your booking. All payment to be made before the date.

We have an exciting programme covering a variety of spiritual learnings.

Yoga and meditation for you to relax
Ortho-Bionomy Breathing
Energetic Fields and Protection
Energy Work
Exploring and enhancing your Spiritual abilities
and more

Upon arrival you will be gifted a workbook to fill in your learnings and reflection, this is a great way when you get home to tap back refreshing and reflecting how far you have come in the following days, weeks and months. It’s how we grow…


Ari: ari.true.essence@gmail.com

Tiffany: Beingwithspirit@gmail.com

Ari: 022 369 8462
Tiffany: 021 738 437

KUTC Junior Club Nights, 𝐅𝐑𝐄𝐄 𝐅𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝐟𝐮𝐧, 𝐟𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐬 𝐚𝐭 𝐊𝐔𝐓𝐂 �
Junior Club Nights at KUTC kick off for the new term this coming Friday – 30th January from 5.30 to 7.00pm. All junior players are welcome – you don’t have to be a KUTC member. Come along to the club at 16 Campbell Street and enjoy some free tennis coaching in a fun environment and snag a sausage or two.
Darren Ward and his friendly team from Cyperus Tennis + Fitness will be on hand to share their tennis skills and tips, whether you’re a beginner or starting to play competitively. You can find out more about Cyperus Tennis +Fitness here: http://www.cyperus.co.nz .
Parent/caregiver volunteers would be welcomed to assist with sausage sizzling. Please DM if you're willing to share your skills.�
Hope to see you there!

description:
New Year, New Venue, January Club Comp 2026 :-), New Year, New Venue, January Club Comp 2026 :-)
When: Saturday 31st January 2026

Where: Weights room, Upper Hutt College, Moonshine Road, Trentham, Upper Hutt.

Entries are limited.

Weigh In: 9am.

Competition Start: 10am.

Entries are limited to 10 lifters, once priority spots are filled, all others will be waitlisted.

Priority will be given to Upper Hutt College students and 41° Lifters.

Sign up is via the Weightlifting NZ website calendar, make sure you select 2026 to find the entry link, entries open Nov 24th. https://weightlifting.nz/Calendar

Cost: $20 per lifter. This fee must be paid as you register via the WNZ site. (This change is to simplify the process now being followed by the club as required by WNZ)

Spectators are FREE.

Live Stream is also FREE so don't sign up anywhere else.

Detailed start list will be released closer to the date on the 41° WLC Facebook page

Registrations for this competition close at noon on the Wednesday prior to the comp, if not full before, so please sign up as soon as possible.

Any questions then please send them to Matt or contact Matt on 027-2322-701.

We are back running club comps this year, so get amongst it :-)

description:
Race to the Brewery 2026, Race to the Brewery 2026
** SAVE THE DATE **

Race to the Brewery 2026 returns to Manawatū for its 16th event!

Race day starts at Property Brokers on Broadway Avenue and finishes at the Tui Brewery in Mangatainoka after six legs of hard slog through the countryside.

This is a fantastic race for businesses, colleagues, and mates to compete in and a great day raising much-needed funds for local charities, including the Manawatū Cancer Society, Rescue Helicopter, and our local volunteer fire brigades.

So whether you're a team or a solo competitor, competitive, or just passionate about putting in the mahi to support local Manawatū charities – the Race to the Brewery is an event you don't want to miss.

🟠 Registrations opening October 2025. Save the Date!
